articles.title: North Korea’s naval buildup poses new security challenges for US, South Korea: expert
articles.excerpt: Questions remain over Pyongyang’s ability to sustain its warships amid vulnerabilities and rising costs.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean .
North Korea’s push to build increasingly large warships could pose new security challenges for South Korea and the United States, but questions remain over whether Pyongyang has the military capabilities and financial resources to operate the ships effectively, security experts told Radio Free Asia.
North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un has made naval modernization a priority, commissioning two 5,000-ton destroyers this year while pursuing even larger surface combatants.
The first destroyer, the Choe Hyon, entered service in June, followed by the Kang Kon in September. During a Nov. 2 visit to the Nampo shipyard, southwest of the capital Pyongyang, Kim inspected what state media described as an enormous new warship, with photographs revealing part of its lower hull.
The destroyers mark a significant departure from North Korea’s traditionally coastal-focused navy, which has relied heavily on smaller vessels. The new larger ships are designed to carry a wider range of weapons, including missiles capable of striking targets at greater distances.
North Korea also conducted tests of new torpedoes in October and November, underscoring Pyongyang’s efforts to expand its naval capabilities.
This picture taken on July 3, 2026 and released by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) via KNS on July 5, 2026 shows North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un (C) observing performance tests of the main weapons systems of the destroyer Kang Kon at an undisclosed location in North Korea.
(STR/KCNA via KNS/AFP) Unlike land-based missile launchers, warships can move across large maritime areas, potentially giving North Korea more options for launching strikes and complicating efforts to track nuclear weapons within the isolated country.
Bruce Bennett, a former senior researcher at the California-based RAND Corporation, told RFA Korean that the destroyers could add another dimension to North Korea’s nuclear threat.
“North Korea is diversifying its means for delivering nuclear weapons. … Its destroyers are designed to carry nuclear weapons, and they will likely do so as part of this diversification process,” said Bennett. “By doing so, it hopes to make it very difficult for the United States to carry out a disarming attack on its nuclear forces. It will have too many targets of too many different types.”
A senior officer in Japan’s Maritime Self-Defense Force, who spoke to RFA Korean on condition of anonymity, also said the destroyers could carry tactical nuclear weapons, increasing the threat posed by Pyongyang’s expanding fleet.
The officer noted that North Korea had likely relied on Chinese and Russian technology to build the destroyers, which appear to be beyond its existing capabilities.
The destroyers’ hulls resemble China’s Type 052D Luyang III-class destroyers, while their radar systems resemble those of Russia’s Admiral Gorshkov-class frigates, suggesting Pyongyang may have drawn on Chinese shipbuilding expertise and Russian weapons technology, according to the officer.
Despite their potential threat, however, the vessels face significant operational limitations, particularly against aircraft and submarines, the officer said.
“Large surface vessels are exposed to threats from the air and underwater. Surface warships cannot operate independently,” the officer said.
Modern naval operations require multiple layers of protection, including onboard air defense systems, early warning aircraft and fighter jets capable of intercepting incoming threats.
North Korea tested an airborne early warning aircraft in March 2025, but South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said at the time that its operational threat remained limited despite potential improvements in surveillance capabilities.
Pyongyang’s fighter fleet also faces disadvantages. In December 2024, U.S. Indo-Pacific Command chief Adm. Samuel Paparo raised the possibility that North Korea could acquire MiG-29 and Su-27 fighter jets.
However, both are fourth-generation aircraft that would face significant challenges against the more advanced fifth-generation F-35 fighters operated by South Korea and the United States, potentially limiting Pyongyang’s ability to protect its warships.
The Japanese officer also questioned the destroyers’ ability to counter submarines, particularly in the complex waters east of the Korean Peninsula.
“The Sea of Japan is an extremely difficult area in which to detect submarines because of its complex currents and salinity distribution,” said the officer, referring to the body of water east of the Korean Peninsula, also known as the East Sea.
“Without combining patrol aircraft such as the P-3C or P-8, it is impossible to locate submarines. North Korean destroyers would not be able to defend themselves against submarine attacks.”
The officer added that even stealth-designed warships could be quickly detected by satellites or high-altitude reconnaissance drones.
This picture taken on Sept. 6, 2026 and released by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on Sept. 7, 2026 shows North Korean leader Kim Jong Un (C on platform) seeing off the destroyer "Kang Kon" duing a commissioning ceremony was held at Wonsan Port in Kangwon Province.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) Political ambitions and mounting costs
Despite those challenges, Kim appears determined to build vessels even larger than Choe Hyon and Kang Kon, reflecting a longstanding North Korean ambition to develop a powerful navy.
That ambition dates back to the reign of Kim’s late grandfather, national founder Kim Il Sung. Pyongyang has long viewed its naval inferiority as a strategic disadvantage, believing it left the country unable to challenge the Northern Limit Line, a disputed maritime boundary established by the U.N. Command after the 1953 Korean War armistice, that places several islands near North Korea’s shore under South Korean control.
But a Japanese government official, who spoke to RFA Korean on condition of anonymity, suggested the younger Kim’s pursuit of increasingly large vessels may reflect personal ambition rather than purely military requirements.
“This may reflect Chairman Kim’s personal desire to possess enormous warships,” the official said.
The official argued that North Korea’s centralized political system could encourage military planners to prioritize the leader’s preferences over operational considerations.
“I believe Kim – who aspires to match countries such as South Korea and the United States – has become fixated on building impressive-looking large warships, so he has issued orders that disregard military rationality,” the official said.
The official added that North Korean military officers and engineers faced pressure to satisfy the leadership, with those opposing Kim’s views risking punishment.
Lee Hyun-ju, who was once Seoul’s consul general in Osaka and who previously headed the South Korean office of the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization, or KEDO, told RFA that military officers in North Korea know that the wisest course of action is to demonstrate loyalty and respect toward Kim Jong Un.
“They also know that displaying intense hatred and aggression toward anyone who insults the supreme leader is the safest approach,” he added.
Beyond their operational limitations, the warships could impose substantial financial costs on North Korea’s economy.
The expense comes as North Korea continues to face international sanctions imposed over its nuclear and missile programs, restricting its access to foreign markets and technology.
According to Japan Self-Defense Forces officials, building a 5,000-ton destroyer would cost at least 50 billion yen (US$314.2 million), even after accounting for the country’s relatively low labor costs.
That would be roughly equivalent to North Korea’s total exports in 2024, according to the officials’ estimate.
“Building a destroyer also requires spending on maintenance, repairs and other operating costs,” a Self-Defense Forces official told RFA Korean. “This would represent a considerable burden for North Korea.”
Edited by Taejun Kang and Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Apple tightens Mac security as AI agents seek your files
articles.excerpt: Apple's macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds new Mac security controls for AI agents, letting you pick specific protected folders instead…
articles.fullText:
Ever download an app on your Mac and click through the permission requests without giving them much thought? You're certainly not alone. But what if one of those approvals gave an AI assistant access to your private messages, financial documents or even files you thought were protected?
That's the concern behind Apple's latest Mac security controls . As AI agents become more capable of performing tasks on your computer, they're also requesting access to more personal information. And once you grant certain permissions, an app could potentially see far more than you intended.
Now, Apple is introducing new protections in macOS 27.3 that give you greater control over what these apps can access . The changes arrived in macOS 27.3 beta 2 on Nov. 16, with the broader software release still to come. Here's what Apple is changing and why you may want to check your Mac's privacy settings now.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
MALICIOUS BROWSER EXTENSIONS CAN HIJACK AI ASSISTANTS
AI assistants have become increasingly useful, especially when you want help getting through a long list of tasks. An AI agent can go further by interacting with apps and taking actions on your behalf. For example, you might ask an AI agent to organize your Downloads folder or find a receipt buried in your email. To complete those tasks, the software may request permission to access information stored on your Mac. That's where things can get uncomfortable. Some apps request a powerful macOS permission called Full Disk Access , which can give them access to nearly everything stored on your computer, including information from other apps.
Apple warns that an app with this permission can read or modify sensitive files. It may also be able to delete or export information without asking you again. And the potential exposure goes beyond documents . Another powerful permission, called System & App Protection Override , can allow an app to control your Mac and monitor activity, including keystrokes, when you grant unrestricted access. That's a lot of trust to place in software, especially when an AI agent can take actions without asking you to approve every step.
Apple's upcoming update introduces several changes designed to make powerful permissions easier to understand. It also gives Mac owners more opportunities to limit access before an app starts working.
Apple is separating its existing Device Control and Data Access permission system into two settings: System & App Protection Override and Accessibility . The change helps clarify when an app is requesting permission to bypass built-in protections. Apple is also introducing more detailed warnings about the information an app could access if you approve its request. Instead of clicking through a vague permission prompt, you'll have more information about what you're allowing.
One of the biggest changes involves Full Disk Access . Starting with macOS 27.3, some apps requesting this permission will let you choose specific protected folders instead of granting access to everything. Other apps may continue using the existing approval process, depending on their purpose.
For example, an AI tool helping you organize work documents may only need access to one folder. You could grant that limited permission while keeping other protected information off-limits. Apple is also introducing a more consistent process for granting these permissions. You'll select the requesting app from a list rather than navigating different approval methods.
Another important addition gives you more control over how AI agents interact with other apps . When configuring System & App Protection Override , you can choose which apps an AI tool may control. For each approved app, you can select Ask First or At Any Time . Choosing Ask First means the AI agent must request permission before controlling that app. That extra confirmation may slow down some automated tasks, but it also gives you an opportunity to catch unwanted actions.
Apple is adding a transparency indicator that appears when an app controls another app through this permission system. That could make it easier to recognize when software is acting on your behalf.
MAC MALWARE CAN HIDE COMMANDS IN YOUR ICLOUD CALENDAR
Apple's announcement follows growing scrutiny over how much information AI-powered software can access. In September, a journalist claimed that Meta's Muse AI app had read his private messages without his permission. Meta disputed that account, saying the Messages integration requires explicit permission. Separately, a security vulnerability in OpenAI's ChatGPT Mac app could have allowed attackers to access sensitive information. OpenAI patched the flaw before it was publicly reported.
These incidents highlight the security concerns surrounding increasingly capable AI software. Even legitimate applications can create privacy risks when they receive broad access to personal information. Apple's response focuses on making those permissions more visible and giving people greater control over what they approve. Importantly, the changes won't prevent you from installing AI agents or using apps that genuinely need broader permissions.
There's something worth knowing before assuming the update will automatically protect everything on your Mac. Apple says permissions you've already granted will remain in effect after the update. The new approval experience primarily applies when apps request permissions going forward.
That means an AI app you installed months ago could still have access to information you previously approved. You'll need to review those permissions yourself if you want to change them. Apple is also allowing developers of certain backup and accessibility applications to request special permissions that preserve their existing functionality. This should help prevent legitimate tools from losing features they need to operate.
You can review your Mac's privacy permissions now, even before macOS 27.3 becomes widely available.
Steps may vary slightly depending on your version of macOS.
If you find an app with permissions it no longer needs, you can revoke its access. Depending on your macOS version, you may see a toggle or an option to remove the app from the permission list. For macOS 27.3: Select an app and click the Remove (−) button to revoke access. To replace broad access with a more limited permission, remove the app and add it again. When prompted, choose the specific protected folders or apps it needs.
Keep in mind that some legitimate applications, including backup software and security tools, require extensive access to function properly. Removing their permissions could prevent certain features from working.
AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU
You don't have to stop using AI assistants to protect your information. A few precautions can help you take advantage of these tools while reducing unnecessary exposure.
When an app requests access to your files, consider whether it needs permission to browse your entire Mac. If the new macOS controls offer a Choose Folder or Choose Apps option, use it to limit the information the software can reach. You can adjust those permissions later if the app needs additional access.
If you're using macOS 27.3, look for the Ask First setting when granting an AI agent permission to control another application. This gives you another opportunity to review what the software wants to do. It's especially useful when an AI tool interacts with apps containing sensitive personal information.
Be careful when installing new AI agents, particularly from unfamiliar websites. We've previously reported how AI-related scams target Mac owners through convincing fake download pages. Stick with official developer websites or the Mac App Store whenever possible. Keep your installed apps updated to receive security fixes.
Your Mac includes built-in malware protection, but reputable antivirus software can add another layer of security. It can help detect malicious downloads and other threats, including malware disguised as legitimate AI tools. However, antivirus software can't reliably prevent an app from accessing information you've already given it permission to use. That's why reviewing your Mac's privacy settings remains important. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
Even when an app has limited access to your files, you should understand how it handles information you choose to share. Check whether the developer stores your data or sends it to cloud servers. Apple's permission controls can restrict access to protected information on your Mac, but they don't replace an app's privacy policy.
An AI tool may have needed access to a particular folder when you first installed it. That doesn't mean it needs the same permission indefinitely. Periodically check Privacy & Security and remove access that no longer serves a purpose. This is particularly important for AI apps you rarely use.
If you're allowing an AI agent to organize or modify files, make sure you have a recent backup. An automated task could accidentally delete something important or change a document you wanted to keep. Apple's built-in Time Machine can automatically back up your Mac and help you recover files if something goes wrong. For step-by-step instructions, check out our guide on how to back up your computer.
I'm glad Apple is taking a closer look at how much access AI agents can have on our computers. These tools are becoming more capable, and I can see why people would want an assistant that handles repetitive work. But giving an app permission to see everything on your Mac seems like a steep price to pay for convenience. I particularly like the option to make an AI agent ask before controlling another app. That's a level of oversight I would want, especially when personal information is involved. My biggest concern is that previously granted permissions will remain active. Apple can introduce better warnings, but those warnings won't change the decisions you've already made. I'd encourage Mac owners to spend a few minutes reviewing their settings rather than waiting for the next update.
Would you trust an AI assistant with unrestricted access to your Mac if it could save you hours of work, or does the thought of software reading your private information cross a line? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: FS meets UK business leaders
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan yesterday led a Hong Kong business, trade, and innovation and technology (I&T) delegation as it continued…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan yesterday led a Hong Kong business, trade, and innovation and technology (I&T) delegation as it continued its visit to the UK.

In London, he met members of the local business and financial sectors to brief them on the latest developments in Hong Kong and explore opportunities for co-operation between Hong Kong and the UK in finance, I&T, and professional services.

Addressing the 22nd Plenary Session of the Hong Kong-Europe Business Council, Mr Chan briefed the participants on Hong Kong’s latest economic developments. He said that the city’s merchandise exports had shown strong growth, consumption and investment had both increased, and the stock market had seen active trading while continuing to attract capital from the Mainland and overseas.

He added that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan sets out its development priorities and direction for the coming half-decade, giving businesses greater certainty as they invest and expand there.

Describing the Northern Metropolis as a key base for Hong Kong’s I&T development, Mr Chan noted that infrastructure projects in the area will bring new opportunities for European investors and professional services firms.

Hong Kong will further enhance its listing regime to channel capital into industries such as artificial intelligence (AI) and biotechnology. He also encouraged European businesses to join hands with their Hong Kong counterparts to support Mainland enterprises expanding overseas by providing them with professional services.

Mr Chan then called on Chinese Ambassador to the UK Zheng Zeguang to update him on the delegation’s programme and Hong Kong’s latest economic and financial outlook. They also had an in-depth exchange on the international landscape, China-UK relations, economic conditions in the UK and Europe, and the expansion of Mainland enterprises into Britain.

At noon, Mr Chan spoke at a luncheon hosted by the Hong Kong Association and exchanged views with members and guests. He emphasised that a key goal of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan is to accelerate its development as an international I&T hub, adding that the city can help UK companies bring technologies to the Mainland while connecting them with local partners. British firms can raise funds, conduct research, and test new technologies in Hong Kong, while drawing on the advanced manufacturing capabilities of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) to turn research outcomes into products.

Mr Chan outlined four areas for closer I&T co-operation between Hong Kong and the UK.

First, UK universities could establish joint laboratories with Hong Kong institutions or set up campuses in the Northern Metropolis. Second, British companies could use the city as a base for their Asian operations. Life and health technology firms, for example, could establish research and development teams in the Loop to conduct cross-boundary clinical trials and develop new drugs.

Third, UK professional services firms could help Hong Kong-based Mainland technology companies obtain product certification and enter the UK and European markets. Fourth, British funds, university endowments, and corporate investors could co-invest with the Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited.

He invited participants to visit the Northern Metropolis and expressed hope that the Association would continue to bring businesses from both places together to foster further co-operation.

Mr Chan then addressed a roundtable on digital assets organised by TheCityUK, a UK financial industry body. He outlined the policy principles and measures guiding the regulation and growth of digital assets in Hong Kong, as well as the latest trends in stablecoins and tokenisation. He also exchanged views with representatives of the local financial sector on market evolution in both jurisdictions, and explored opportunities for their financial institutions to work together in this area.

In the evening, Mr Chan spoke at the 40th Hong Kong Dinner in London organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council. He said that, according to UK government figures, bilateral trade reached £33 billion in the year to June, up 23% year on year. Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s economy expanded by 5.1% over the first nine months of this year, with the Government forecasting full-year growth of 4.8%.

Mr Chan highlighted that Hong Kong promotes AI as a core industry while supporting its adoption across other sectors. He drew a distinction between using AI and building a business around it: a company that simply uses AI does things faster, whereas an AI-native firm rebuilds its products, organisation, and operating model.

Citing medical technology as an example of Hong Kong-UK co-operation, Mr Chan said that surgical robots developed by Cornerstone Robotics – a Hong Kong company founded by a professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong – are now operating in National Health Service hospitals in Portsmouth and east London. He added that approximately a dozen InnoHK laboratories in the city are run with British institutions, such as the University of Cambridge, the University of Oxford, Imperial College London, and University College London.

He welcomed British universities, laboratories, and innovative companies to participate in the development of the Northern Metropolis. Three university towns covering over 1,000 hectares are being built there – with about 300 hectares for campuses and the rest for laboratories, technology parks, industry, and housing – to bring together the combined strengths of education, research, and industry, he said.

Mr Chan said that what the GBA brings together globally includes not only goods and services, but also technology, capital, talent, advanced manufacturing, and the know-how to take research to market. He noted that as Mainland enterprises invest in the UK and Europe, bankers, lawyers, accountants, and advisers in Hong Kong and London can work together to help them establish and expand their operations.

On financial markets, Mr Chan said that Hong Kong and London can deepen ties in offshore Renminbi (RMB) business and gold trading. He remarked that as the world’s largest offshore RMB centre and the leading centre outside Asia respectively, the two cities span the trading day and have strong grounds to link their markets more closely.

Mr Chan added that Hong Kong is building a complete gold value chain – covering trading, clearing, storage, and delivery – ahead of the formal launch of its central gold clearing system early next year, while exploring co-operation on delivery standards with the London Bullion Market Association.

He concluded that Britain has long been part of the Hong Kong story, and that new investment continues to renew the ties between the two places.

Mr Chan will lead the delegation to the Netherlands today to continue the visit.

articles.title: CE visits Wang Fuk Court residents
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee recently visited residents affected by the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po who are temporarily…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee recently visited residents affected by the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po who are temporarily staying in Aberdeen to check on their well-being and the progress of their new housing arrangements. He was joined on last Saturday’s visit by Secretary for Home & Youth Affairs Alice Mak and Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun.

Residents from two households who expect to move into their new units next month told Mr Lee the properties suited their needs. They added that moving in earlier had greatly eased their minds.

They thanked the Government for its help, including support from the “one social worker per household” scheme and the District Services & Community Care Teams with financial assistance, document replacement and medical arrangements. They also backed the Government’s push for systemic reforms and its fight against bid-rigging.

Mr Lee said the Government is deeply saddened by the suffering caused by the fire and will continue to do everything possible to support Wang Fuk Court residents.

“Through the ‘one social worker per household’ mechanism and the Care Teams, we will continue to follow up comprehensively on residents’ needs in relation to supplies, medical care, emotional support and assistance in choosing new accommodation. We will continue to stand by the residents and provide them with appropriate support to help them start a new life,” he said.

Mr Lee reiterated that the Government is speeding up long-term housing plans to help residents rebuild their lives quickly. At the same time, it is amending six laws to close loopholes in building maintenance and renovation works so similar incidents do not happen again.

He stressed that these legal changes will stop criminals and syndicates from exploiting building maintenance and renovation projects for unlawful gain. This will address public concerns about fraud in building repairs.

The Chief Executive has instructed officials to put residents first, review every stage of building maintenance and renovation and swiftly finish drafting the legislative amendments for the Legislative Council’s scrutiny to strengthen regulation.

The Government also thanked the Tung Wah Group of Hospitals for offering free legal services to help with property purchase matters.

articles.title: Drug formulary to launch on Dec 30
articles.excerpt: The Health Bureau announced today that the Community Drug Formulary (CDF) will be launched on December 30. From that date…
articles.fullText:
The Health Bureau announced today that the Community Drug Formulary (CDF) will be launched on December 30. From that date, family doctors under the Primary Healthcare Co-care Network will prescribe drugs from the CDF instead of the current basic-tier drug list.

The CDF expands drug coverage to include medications in more disease categories, with patient drug co-payments for newly added drugs costing only about one-tenth to one-third of market prices. Coupled with the drug co-payment subsidy introduced by the Government for Co-care Network participants, the formulary will alleviate long-term medication expenses for chronic disease patients.

The CDF covers a total of 151 drugs, including 38 newly added drug items. Coverage is expanded beyond the current eight chronic diseases, such as diabetes mellitus and hypertension, and 11 episodic illnesses, which include upper respiratory tract infection and gastroenteritis, to encompass disease categories such as urology, ophthalmology and dermatology.

The Government will review the CDF periodically, with a long-term goal of covering up to 200 to 400 drug items.

The CDF comprises three tiers. Tier 1 consists of 146 non-patented drugs and Tier 2 of five patented drugs. Tier 3 is a special category with no drugs being introduced at this stage.

The Government will provide an annual drug co-payment subsidy of $200 for each co-care network participant to directly offset Tier 1 drug expenses. The subsidy is valid for the current year only, and any unused balance will not be carried forward to the following year. Patients will receive SMS notifications confirming details of their co-payments and subsidy deductions. Eligible elderly people under the co-care network can also use their Elderly Health Care Vouchers.

Currently, around 70,000 patients who have completed screening for the “three highs” – high blood pressure, high blood sugar, and high blood lipids – or chronic hepatitis B, and who have3 entered treatment under the co-care network will be the first to benefit from the CDF.

In the media briefing today, Commissioner for Primary Healthcare Dr Pang Fei-chau highlighted that the CDF demonstrates the Government’s strong commitment to developing primary healthcare services in the community, and to giving citizens access to affordable drugs for chronic diseases and episodic illnesses.

He said: “We will try to lower the market prices of the drugs for major chronic diseases that we hope the citizens can get the service for in the community.

“We will try to use different methods to do it, including the tendering process, so that we can have a better drug price for the people. When they have a chronic disease, they can have more affordable conditions to follow up in the private sector.”

articles.title: GBA legal conference held in Macau
articles.excerpt: Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan today led a delegation to Macau to attend the eighth Greater Bay Area (GBA)…
articles.fullText:
Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan today led a delegation to Macau to attend the eighth Greater Bay Area (GBA) Legal Departments Joint Conference.

Mr Cheung had an in-depth exchange with Guangdong Department of Justice Director-General Chen Xudong and Macao Special Administrative Region Government Secretary for Administration & Justice Wong Sio Chak.

The conference aims to advance the development of the rule of law in the GBA through the collaborative efforts of the three sides.

During the conference, representatives from the legal departments of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macau held in-depth discussions on key areas including mediation, arbitration, legislative collaboration, and the nurturing of legal talent.

They have yielded phased achievements in formulating and promoting GBA standards, further strengthening their work on aligning mechanisms and rules.

The three places have officially launched the "Platform for Promotion of the GBA Standards on Arbitration & Mediation".

The first batch of more than 10 arbitration and mediation institutions has joined the platform. They will work closely with the joint conference to promote the relevant GBA standards and gather feedback from the sectors and users.

The initiative aims to facilitate the alignment of arbitration and mediation mechanisms among the three places and continuously improve the relevant standards.

Dr Cheung said the mechanisms for the GBA standards on arbitration and mediation will become more comprehensive upon the platform’s establishment, covering the formulation, promotion, and refinement of standards. Hence, he added, these benchmarks are not only created, but also put into practice and continuously optimised at the same time.

In addition, Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macau have agreed to press ahead with research on legislative collaboration.

Dr Cheung said the “Task Force on Expediting the Alignment of Rules & Mechanisms in Guangdong, Hong Kong & Macau”, which he leads, is currently being formed. It will co-ordinate with relevant bureaus and support the joint conference’s work.

The conference also endorsed the GBA Mediator Panel 2026, and the three parties took the opportunity to exchange views on the usage of the GBA Arbitrator Panel.

articles.title: LCSD follows up on URBTIX incident
articles.excerpt: The Leisure & Cultural Services Department confirmed today that, as reported by the URBTIX system contractor yesterday, the system was…
articles.fullText:
The Leisure & Cultural Services Department confirmed today that, as reported by the URBTIX system contractor yesterday, the system was illegally accessed in a hacking incident.

Upon discovering the incident, the contractor said it took immediate measures to stop the hack and reviewed the system to ensure its normal operation.

The URBTIX system was developed and is owned by the contractor at its own cost. It mainly provides ticketing services for the department's performance venues.

Preliminary findings suggest that the incident involves the personal data of around 1,300,000 users, including usernames or names, telephone numbers and email addresses. The system does not collect information on users' identity documents and masks credit card information.

The department said it is highly concerned about the incident and has asked the contractor to conduct a detailed investigation and submit a report. It has also reported the matter to the Police Force, the Security Bureau, the Digital Policy Office (DPO) and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD).

Additionally, the department and the contractor are making arrangements to inform people affected. The department is also consulting the PCPD and the DPO in conducting a comprehensive review of the incident with the contractor, with a view to strengthening protection measures for the system and preventing the recurrence of similar incidents.

articles.title: Bill passed for half-rate trading tax
articles.excerpt: The Government has welcomed the Legislative Council’s passage today of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Tax Concessions for Shipping-related Activities &…
articles.fullText:
The Government has welcomed the Legislative Council’s passage today of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Tax Concessions for Shipping-related Activities & Physical Commodity Trading) Bill 2026, which introduces a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity trading and enhances existing tax concessions for shipping-related activities.

The amendment ordinance will be published in the Government Gazette on December 4. The relevant tax concessions will apply to qualifying profits from years of assessment beginning on or after April 1, 2025.

The new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity trading is designed to attract commodity traders to establish a presence in Hong Kong. Where a qualifying trader has incurred expenditure on “specified maritime services”, a certain proportion of such expenditure is required to be spent on Hong Kong service providers, thereby promoting the development of the local maritime services ecosystem.

In response to the evolving international tax landscape under the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting 2.0 framework formulated by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation & Development, the Government’s amendment ordinance introduces an additional 15% concessionary rate under existing preferential tax regimes for shipping-related activities, to ease compliance costs for eligible multinational enterprises.

The bill also introduces tax deduction arrangements aligned with international tax standards, thereby preserving the competitiveness of Hong Kong’s tax regimes. Commodity traders under the new regime are also offered the abovementioned additional 15% concessionary tax rate option.

The Government highlighted that it is pressing ahead with the “volume to value” transformation of the Hong Kong Port, as set out in the National 15th Five-Year Plan and Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

It added that it is developing the city into a global maritime capital in all respects, anchored by the dual-core strategy of “enhancing port competitiveness” and “optimising the high value-added maritime services ecosystem”. It considers a favourable tax regime a core pillar and key source of competitiveness, and essential for sustaining the growth momentum of the city’s high value-added maritime services industry.

The Government said it will actively promote the new tax concession locally and overseas. To help the industry understand the new requirements, the Inland Revenue Department will issue guidance and maintain close communication with stakeholders to provide technical support and address enquiries.

articles.title: FM calls on UK to uphold principle of free trade
articles.excerpt: China hopes that Britain will uphold the principle of free trade and adopt an open approach, providing Chinese enterprises with…
articles.fullText:
China hopes that Britain will uphold the principle of free trade and adopt an open approach, providing Chinese enterprises with stable policy expectations and a favourable business environment for cooperation in Britain, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Tuesday.

Wang made the remarks during a phone conversation with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband.

China stands ready to work with Britain to promote the mature, steady and sustainable development of bilateral relations, Wang added.

The foreign minister also said he hopes that London will earnestly abide by the one-China principle and uphold the political foundation of bilateral relations. (Reporting by Xinhua)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Shanghai Party chief Chen Jining under investigation
articles.excerpt: Shanghai's Communist Party chief Chen Jining, who's also a Politburo member, is under disciplinary and supervisory investigation, an official statement…
articles.fullText:
Shanghai's Communist Party chief Chen Jining, who's also a Politburo member, is under disciplinary and supervisory investigation, an official statement said on Tuesday.

Chen is being investigated by the Communist Party of China Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision for suspected severe violations of discipline and laws, the statement said.

Chen, 62, was previously president of Tsinghua University.

He became environmental protection minister in 2015 and then served as mayor of Beijing.

He joined the Politburo in 2022 and was named Party boss of Shanghai. (Xinhua and agencies)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Gleneagles Hospital reports patient data leak
articles.excerpt: Gleneagles Hospital has reported an incident of data breach involving patient information. Health authorities said they were notified by the…
articles.fullText:
Gleneagles Hospital has reported an incident of data breach involving patient information.

Health authorities said they were notified by the private hospital in Wong Chuk Hang on Monday of unauthorised activity in the security infrastructure of its mobile application, My Gleneagles SmartHealth.

"According to the information provided by the hospital, the hospital discovered on November 18 that unauthorised activity involving the security infrastructure supporting its patient mobile application, My Gleneagles SmartHealth, resulting in unauthorised access to certain patients' and other personal data," the Department of Health said in a statement.

"The hospital stated that it has engaged independent cybersecurity experts to conduct an investigation, has notified relevant law enforcement and regulatory authorities, and will inform the affected patients."

In a statement, Gleneagles said it had isolated the affected access route right away and taken the app offline as a precaution, adding that the incident was contained.

The Health Bureau said it has suspended the hospital's registration on the Electronic Health System (eHealth) following the leak.

During the suspension, the hospital is unable to access or provide patients’ electronic health records, to ensure the eHealth system’s security and integrity.

The bureau said the hospital's mobile application has no direct connection to eHealth, and that the eHealth system has maintained normal operation, with no evidence showing it has been compromised or any personal information has been leaked.

Authorities will determine if Gleneagles has contravened the Private Healthcare Facilities Ordinance or the Code of Practice for Private Hospitals, and take necessary actions.

The Department of Health has asked the hospital to submit a detailed investigation report within four weeks.

The department said it will continue to follow up on the case.

Edited by Edmond Fong
