articles.title: 7.9pc increase in HK Electric tariffs, 1.8pc for CLP
articles.excerpt: The people of Hong Kong will have to dig deeper into their pockets for electricity charges from January. Presenting the…
articles.fullText:
The people of Hong Kong will have to dig deeper into their pockets for electricity charges from January.

Presenting the annual tariff review at a Legco panel meeting on Tuesday, HK Electric, which supplies electricity to Hong Kong Island and Lamma Island, said its net tariff will climb by 7.9 percent.

CLP Power – which serves Kowloon, the New Territories and most outlying islands – will increase its charges by 1.8 percent.

The tariff hikes mean about 12.9 cents more per unit of electricity for HK Electric customers compared with this year, and an additional 2.6 cents for CLP Power households.

Secretary for Environment and Ecology Tse Chin-wan noted that the gap in tariffs between the two power firms was widening due to rising international fuel prices since the start of the Middle East conflict earlier this year, describing it as a structural issue.

The government is determined to address it, Tse added.

“For HK Electric, the market is smaller. There is not a scalable effect. In terms of fuel mix, unlike the CLP – they have nuclear power – HK Electric relies completely on fossil fuel, so they are particularly vulnerable to the surge in fuel cost,” he said.

“We will try to stabilise the tariff in the long run and also reduce the gap between the prices between the two companies.”

Tse also said the government will no longer allow the utility firms to build new fossil fuel energy generators.

Instead, the firms will construct large-scale electricity facilities at Area 132 in Tseung Kwan O to receive zero-carbon electricity from the mainland.

Alan Ng, CLP's senior director of planning and development, said the firm has already allocated HK$250 million from its Community Energy Saving Fund to assist the underprivileged, promote energy saving and decarbonisation, and enhance buildings’ energy efficiency and electrical safety.

HK Electric’s general manager Bill Ho said he expects the fuel market to continue to fluctuate, adding that price trends would be hard to predict.

The firm will try its best to make sure fuel supply would be sufficient and reliable, he added.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HK, mainland slip amid cheer at Huang shot in the arm
articles.excerpt: Mainland stocks lagged a powerful global rally on Tuesday, after Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO fired up AI-related…
articles.fullText:
Mainland stocks lagged a powerful global rally on Tuesday, after Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO fired up AI-related shares, with investors betting the bridging role he played between China and the United States had diminished.

While the move helped reverse part of last week's global equity rout, the boost to mainland and Hong Kong shares was far more muted than the surge seen in South Korea, Japan and the United States.

The benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 164 points, or 0.7 percent, lower at 22,219 on turnover of HK$212.63 billion.

The tech index lost 41 points, or 1.2 percent, to end at 3,466 while the China enterprises index fell 75 points, or one percent, to 7,452.

On the mainland, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended up nine points, or 0.27 percent at 3,548 after falling to its lowest since July 2025 on Monday, with traders saying state investors were buying some key index ETFs to lift the market.

The Shenzhen Component Index closed 30 points, or 0.29 percent, lower at 10,423 while the ChiNext edged down one points, or 0.05 percent, to 2,278.

Even some of the AI-linked winners struggled to hold their gains.

The 5G Communication Index rose as much as seven percent in early trade before trimming its advance to 1.2 percent by market close, while Zhongji Innolight, an Nvidia supplier of optical transceivers, surged as much as 12 percent before giving up all of its gains.

"This is definitely a shot in the arm, as you can see from this morning's trading," said Zeng Wenkai, chief investment officer at Hong Kong-based Shengqi Capital.

"But A-shares and Hong Kong stocks follow their own patterns, independent of global markets, so it still comes down to how forcefully the 'national team' steps in to support the market this time," he said, referring to China's state-backed investors that buy stocks to stabilise markets.

Mainland stocks have fallen more than 10 percent this year, breaking a two-year rally that began when stimulus pledges sent shares soaring, and stalling Beijing's efforts to break a long-standing boom-bust cycle in favour of a "slow bull" market that delivers steady returns.

Regulators have also moved to shore up sentiment, with China's three main exchanges announcing on Sunday a package of market-support measures, including easier margin-financing rules.

Zeng Wanping, a fund manager at Beijing Monolith Fund Management, said Huang's return would benefit Chinese firms in Nvidia's supply chain, but the United States would not relax chip controls against China.

"Huang's return was partly due to the Wall Street slump. It was not designed to rescue China's stock market," he said.

The tech-focused Star50 Index rose just 1.6 percent while memory-chip giant CXMT gained merely one percent.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended nearly 2,208 points, or 3.91 percent, at 58,644, with Nvidia-linked stock surges of 14.89 percent for Murata Manufacturing, 12.45 percent for Advantest and 11.54 percent for Furukawa Electric.

The broader Topix gained 90 points, or 2.47 percent, to end at 3,764.

In Seoul, the Kospi ended surged 297 points, or 6.32 percent, at 5,006, with Nvidia connections paying off in gains of 6.7 percent for Samsung Electronics, 6.73 percent for SK Hynix, 11.1 percent for Hyundai Motor, 15.9 percent for LG Electronics and 4.1 percent for e-commerce firm Naver. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Exiled PM targets December 16 for Bangladesh return
articles.excerpt: Ousted Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on…
articles.fullText:
Ousted Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on December 16, the anniversary of the end of her country's 1971 liberation war with Pakistan, her spokesman said on Tuesday, though the government said she can only return through extradition.

It is the first time Hasina, 79, has set a specific date for her return, potentially raising political and legal tensions in a country where her party is banned and where violence has become deadly since she sought a new passport and other documents this month.

The pressure comes as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, who took office in February, grapples with setbacks including one of the world's worst measles outbreaks and protests by garment workers demanding higher wages.

In addition to seeking the paperwork, cancelled months after she fled to Delhi following the uprising against her, Hasina has urged the Bangladeshi government to arrange her return on flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines.

The government, however, reiterated that she can only be extradited by India, having been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising.

Hasina has denied the charges from exile.

"Hasina is a convicted criminal; a fugitive terrorist," Humaiun Kobir, minister of state for foreign affairs, said.

"She can only return home by extradition treaty; in handcuffs, and under strict surveillance."

On the request to arrange a flight, Kobir said: "Bangladesh will not entertain any such delusional request".

India's foreign ministry said it was examining Bangladesh's request to extradite her and that it wanted to "engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties".

An adviser to Prime Minister Rahman said the government plans to carry out the death sentence if Hasina returns.

"There will be no negotiations with the fugitive Hasina, and Bangladesh will discuss the modalities of her extradition with India," said Zahed Ur Rahman, information adviser to the prime minister.

He said to prevent any Awami League leaders from illegally entering Bangladesh via the partly porous land border with India, "Border Guard Bangladesh remains on alert".

Aminul Islam, chief prosecutor of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal, which sentenced Hasina to death, said it was "ridiculous" for a convicted fugitive to expect the government to arrange her return.

The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced her out of power.

Awami League protesters have increasingly taken to the streets to demand Hasina's return, with demonstrations turning deadly, especially in her ancestral home district of Gopalganj.

"People are no longer staying silent," said Rezwan Howlader, an Awami League youth leader in Gopalganj.

"Despite arrests, pressure and harassment, our leaders and activists remain steadfast and hopeful. No one can erase Sheikh Hasina or the support she enjoys among millions of people waiting to welcome her back to Bangladesh." (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Musk companies take key step closer to mega merger
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk's two public companies have appointed five directors, three from Tesla and two from SpaceX, to guide two special…
articles.fullText:
Elon Musk's two public companies have appointed five directors, three from Tesla and two from SpaceX, to guide two special committees handling merger negotiations, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday.

The directors are Roelof Botha and Randy Glein from SpaceX and Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung from Tesla, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.

Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month that a merger unifying his AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions under a single corporate roof would be "a good idea".

He confirmed the companies had formed special committees of independent directors to discuss a union.

The special committees have hired advisers who are fine-tuning financial models that will form the basis for their negotiating positions in an all-stock merger, including Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs for SpaceX and Evercore for Tesla, the report said.

The bankers are studying which parts of the proposed conglomerate overlap, even as a potential combination faces steep ⁠regulatory hurdles over SpaceX's US defence contracts and Tesla's reliance on China.

Bloomberg reported earlier this month that a deal could be announced as early as December, citing progress in merger negotiations. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Huawei passes 100m mark in HarmonyOS takeup
articles.excerpt: Huawei on Tuesday announced that the number of smartphones, tablets and computers running its self-developed HarmonyOS operating system has exceeded…
articles.fullText:
Huawei on Tuesday announced that the number of smartphones, tablets and computers running its self-developed HarmonyOS operating system has exceeded 100 million, marking a major milestone in the company's efforts to build an independent software ecosystem.

The figure covers devices running HarmonyOS 5, 6 and 7.

The HarmonyOS operating system now offers more than 460,000 applications and services, with over 12 million registered developers, it said.

Huawei introduced a new HarmonyOS architecture in October 2024, with the launch of HarmonyOS 5, followed by subsequent updates, versions 6 and 7.

The architecture is independent of Google's Android and Apple's iOS, featuring its own operating kernel, programming language and AI framework, all developed without using the Linux kernel or Android open-source code.

Operating systems are the foundation of the digital ecosystem, while the number of devices running them is a key factor determining whether an ecosystem can achieve sufficient scale to take root and sustain itself.

It took about 25 months for the self-developed HarmonyOS to grow from commercial launch to surpassing the 100-million-devices milestone.

Huawei said HarmonyOS applications now cover a wide range of areas, including local services, e-commerce retail, office work, travel and video games.

New applications combining innovative technology with real-world use cases have emerged, from high-definition livestreaming with telephoto macro photography to accessibility tools for people with language barriers.

More than 14,000 contributors are developing industry-specific innovations on the open-source OpenHarmony operating system, producing over 120 customised versions for sectors such as power, water management and manufacturing.

Xia Yubin, director of the OpenHarmony technology club at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, said operating systems have long been dominated by a few foreign companies, and HarmonyOS' surpassing of the 100-million mark means China's foundational software has blazed a path for independent development that can be replicated.

More devices and more diverse scenarios lead to a more mature ecosystem, which in turn encourages more companies to invest in underlying technological innovation.

Huawei has continued to prioritise research and development.

In the first half of 2026, its R&D spending reached a same-period record high of 121.38 billion yuan, up 25.2 percent year on year, according to its semi-annual report, with R&D accounting for 25.94 percent of total revenue. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Late pope Francis 'had seen devil three times'
articles.excerpt: The late pope Francis saw the devil three times and once saw the "gates of hell", he revealed in his…
articles.fullText:
The late pope Francis saw the devil three times and once saw the "gates of hell", he revealed in his personal diary, excerpts of which were published on Tuesday in a new book.

"The Private Diary of Pope Francis," by Argentine Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, includes passages taken from a journal the former Jorge Bergoglio kept between 1992 and 2024, a document that reveals his worries, regrets and self-critiques – as well as his enormous humanity and faith.

Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, said he was asked by Francis to help make known to the world the musings inside the black plastic journal.

Upon Francis's death last year, Fernandez expressed concern to his successor, Leo XIV, that the book would be "left forgotten in some storage".

He was allowed to publish passages, noting that "the spiritual concerns present in his [Francis's] heart are very clear and can do us good".

In one of the most intriguing revelations, Francis writes that while archbishop of Buenos Aires, he saw the devil three different times including "from the car while I was going home, and in the choir during the mass", and once in Rome following a visit to Chile.

"I discovered that the demon was prowling brazenly, hovering cunningly," wrote Francis in his journal on January 24, 2021, according to an advance copy of the French-language version of the book.

Francis wrote that he recalled three episodes "where I'm sure he actually appeared physically".

"About 15 years ago. I saw him from the car window. I won't forget his threatening and, at the same time, alluring eyes," he wrote.

During the second episode inside a Carmelite chapel, Francis wrote: "He looked at me with flaming eyes.

"I won't forget that look, more intense than the previous one. They were like flashes of fire."

The third episode occurred during a meeting in Rome, following a visit to Chile.

"I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything... I can't forget the powerful rasp of his voice," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters".

Francis also revealed, on June 7, 2018, that on the night before, while getting ready to go to sleep, he "saw the gates of hell".

"Pagan seduction in all its force. I watched a little, and it terrified me," he said, adding that he "took the rosary as a weapon".

"It's dangerous to get close to the gates of hell, because flames can spring out and burn," he wrote.

Throughout the diary, Francis does not hesitate to criticise himself, for his occasional "feelings of disdain, envy, pride" or for having ignored a drunk man in the street who addressed him "because I wanted to walk in peace and quiet".

"The arrogant, self-sufficient, cynical Jorge who lies to himself," is how he described himself on December 30, 2022.

Mercy is a recurrent theme in the journal.

"In hindsight, I realised all the harm I've caused in my life. How much of the Lord's mercy I need!" he wrote on January 5, 1997.

Pope Francis appeared to worry that his days on Earth would be short-lived, fretting over his ageing and the need to "deal with it".

In 1996, at age 60 – nearly three decades before his death – he wrote: "I want to do good with the little time I have left, hoping to be kind.

"How much time wasted, how much harm done!"

Francis died on April 21, 2025. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: October visitor arrivals spike 12pc to 5.13m
articles.excerpt: Provisional visitor arrivals for October hit about 5.13 million, up 12 percent year on year, the Tourism Board said on…
articles.fullText:
Provisional visitor arrivals for October hit about 5.13 million, up 12 percent year on year, the Tourism Board said on Tuesday, thanks to the National Day Golden Week, a series of mega events and festive celebrations.

"The National Day Golden Week, alongside mega events and festive celebrations such as the International Lantern Spectacular and the Hong Kong Wine & Dine Festival, as well as Mice (Meetings, Incentives, Conventions and Exhibitions) events, sports events and concerts held across the city, attracted a large number of visitors and helped stimulate tourism-related sectors, such as dining, retail and hospitality," it said.

In a statement, the board added that major exhibitions and events held in other Greater Bay Area cities also facilitated regional tourism and business exchanges.

By source market, mainland and long-haul markets continued to perform well, with arrivals from across the border reaching about 3.97 million, up 15 percent, and long-haul arrivals rising 19 percent.

New markets recorded growth of 37 percent, while short-haul markets fell 14 percent, which the board attributed to the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday falling in October last year and affecting the year-on-year comparison.

India recorded significant growth, driven by long weekends and Mice events held in Hong Kong and elsewhere in the Greater Bay Area.

For the first 10 months of the year, cumulative visitor arrivals reached 45.8 million, up 12 percent year on year, reflecting continued steady growth of Hong Kong's tourism industry, the board said.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hong Kong SAR's first astronaut set to return home
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong SAR’s first astronaut, Lai Ka-ying, will return to Earth after completing an in-orbit crew rotation, the China…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong SAR’s first astronaut, Lai Ka-ying, will return to Earth after completing an in-orbit crew rotation, the China Manned Space Agency on Tuesday said, as it announced that the Shenzhou-24 would launch on Wednesday morning to the Tiangong Space Station.

The mission will carry the station’s first foreign astronaut, Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who will fly alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi.

Ali will conduct a short mission and return with Lai and Zhang Zhiyuan, another Shenzhou-23 astronaut who will command the return flight.

Zhang Jingbo, who is a spokesman for the agency, said Lai had completed a range of tasks as payload specialist.

"She did a great job with space science research, tech tests, and science outreach," he said.

"Working closely with her crewmates and ground teams, she ran experiments like studying the molecular mechanisms behind multigeneration genetic stability and environmental adaptability of space-grown rice."

He added that Lai also operated a robotic arm inside the cabin during an extravehicular activity, supporting her two teammates and helping them smoothly complete tasks including solar-wing repair and the installation of space debris protection devices.

Zhang noted that Lai also made a virtual return to her alma mater in September for a live educational lecture that captivated students in Hong Kong and Macao.

"She and her crewmates were the space teachers that made microgravity experiments live for young people and explaining how astronauts do research on the station, giving Hong Kong and Macao folks a direct look at the nation's space achievements and deepening their love for the country. It got a great response," he said.

Zhang said Lai approached every task with vigour and a down-to-earth scientific attitude, and that her experience had given young people — especially Hong Kong and Macao youth — a sense of the strength of the nation’s science and technological capabilities.

He expressed hope that her experience would encourage young people to boldly pursue the nation’s space dreams.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'HK perfect place for Asian maths research body'
articles.excerpt: Setting up the Asian Mathematical Union — the first of its kind in Asia — in Hong Kong would give…
articles.fullText:
Setting up the Asian Mathematical Union — the first of its kind in Asia — in Hong Kong would give a huge boost to the SAR's bid to host an international mathematics congress, an award-winning mathematician said.

Tsinghua University professor Yau Shing-tung — who won mathematics' highest honour, the Fields Medal, in 1982 — will lead the union as its founding president.

An inauguration ceremony for the body was held at the Chinese University of Hong Kong on Tuesday.

Speaking to RTHK, Yau pointed out that Asia had been the only continent without a union to bring its mathematical community together.

He noted the field is growing rapidly across the region and requires a unified platform to connect scholars from different countries to work together.

That is where Hong Kong can step in and serve as a hub to gather mathematicians from across Asia, he stressed.

“Hong Kong is clearly in the middle of Asia. Every country can fly to Hong Kong with no obstruction. Importantly, Hong Kong is basically visa-free. There is not much of a problem applying for a visa to come to Hong Kong,” he said.

“And Hong Kong has established a mathematics community for more than 50 years.

“We also have enough resources, coupled with our motherland ... we can offer a lot of visiting positions and postdoc positions for Asian countries to come here to work together with us.”

In July, Hong Kong lost its bid to host the 2030 International Congress of Mathematicians to Glasgow in Scotland, but Yau stressed that uniting Asia's mathematical community gives the SAR a major boost for future editions.

One of the union’s research directions would be on artificial intelligence, Yau said, emphasising that mathematics is vital for driving technological advancement.

"The parameter that AI encounters is billions and billions of numbers," he said.

"Out of billions and billions of data you need to find the one you want. If you just make an error it will take forever to get the answer. You have to find a mathematical way to help you to get to the answer faster."

Besides AI, Yau noted that the union would focus on three other core research areas: pure mathematics, applied mathematics and statistics.

He said the union plans to invite 100 postdocs and 25 senior faculty members to conduct research in Hong Kong.

Most postdoc positions are reserved for applicants from Asia — with 20 spots dedicated to mathematicians from other parts of the world, Yau added.

They will also gather in Hong Kong each year for a major annual meeting.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Building-upkeep sector warned bid-rigging days over
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Eric Chan urged the building-maintenance trade on Tuesday to abandon bid-rigging entirely – saying they would have no…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Eric Chan urged the building-maintenance trade on Tuesday to abandon bid-rigging entirely – saying they would have no chance of getting away with it – as he highlighted government efforts to crack down on manipulative practices.

Speaking on an RTHK programme, he said two syndicates had been dismantled, more than 160 people arrested and about HK$230 million gains linked to bid-rigging seized as the government moves to criminalise the practice following the Wang Fuk Court fire.

Chan said the fire exposed how common bid-rigging was in the industry – and warned that, beyond undermining fire safety, it directly left owners paying more for poorer-quality work.

On other reforms, he said nearly 30 of the 120 recommendations in the Wang Fuk Court fire inquiry report had already been implemented, with close to 90 percent to be completed by next year.

The reforms, Chan stressed, were driven by a determination to turn grief into action.

"When a tragedy strikes, of course we are deeply saddened, deeply hurt, but how you channel that grief and pain into a driving force for reform, so that the public will, from now on, benefit, and ensure this kind of incident never happens again – that is what we must do," he said.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK rises as region charges up in tech relief
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong and mainland stocks rebounded on Tuesday from more than one-year lows, as Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong and mainland stocks rebounded on Tuesday from more than one-year lows, as Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm sparked a rally in AI-related shares and helped reverse part of last week's global equity selloff.

The Hang Seng Index opened higher by 243 points, or 1.09 percent, to put the benchmark at 22,627.

The China enterprises index was up 59 points, or 0.8 percent, at 7,587 while the tech index surged up 71 points, or 2.05 percent, to 3,579.

The artificial intelligence index opened up six percent.

Up north, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index rose 29 points, or 0.82 percent, to open 3,567.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 254 points, or 2.43 percent, higher at 10,708 while the ChiNext Index climbed 88 points, or 3.88 percent, up to 2,368.

The tech-focused Star50 Index jumped 3.3 percent while the 5G Communication Index surged seven percent.

Memory-chip giant CXMT rose more than six percent.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 573 points, or 1.02 percent, up at 57,009 before accelerating to be 2,167 points higher at one stage before noon,

In Seoul, the Kospi did much better than its Japanese counterpart in opening for the day, leaping 171 points, or 3.64 percent, up to 4,880 before its gains punched up to put the benchmark 306 points up at one stage before lunch.

The rebound marked a sharp turnaround in market sentiment after leadership turmoil at the world's most valuable chip firm and renewed concerns over AI spending had rattled global markets in recent sessions.

"The return of the most important man in the AI industry to the helm of its most important company has eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade, at least at the margins," despite lingering concerns about slowing AI investment and moderating earnings growth, said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China to launch Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Weds
articles.excerpt: The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship will launch at 8.18am on Wednesday morning from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre, the China Manned…
articles.fullText:
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship will launch at 8.18am on Wednesday morning from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced on Tuesday.

A Long March-2F carrier rocket, which will be used for the launch, will soon be filled with propellant, said Zhang Jingbo, the CMSA spokesperson, at a press conference.

Zhang also said 90 scientific experiments and technology tests were being planned for the Shenzhou-24 mission.

These will cover space life sciences, space material science, microgravity fluid physics and combustion science, fundamental physics, space medicine, and new space technologies.

In a first for the country's space programme, the Shenzhou-24 crew will include Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station, as well as Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi.

As a payload specialist, Ali will join in the crew's routine work and focus on joint China-Pakistan space science experiments, primarily installing experiment samples and units and carrying out in-orbit experiments.

The Shenzhou-24 is the eighth crewed mission during the development stage of China's space station, and the 41st flight mission overall of China's manned space programme. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK$630m new support measures for Wang Fuk Court
articles.excerpt: The government announced on Tuesday that two new beginning support grants would be rolled out for residents of Wang Fuk…
articles.fullText:
The government announced on Tuesday that two new beginning support grants would be rolled out for residents of Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, providing further financial support to each flat owner and to families of each deceased resident.

The Support Fund for Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po will provide owners of each flat in Wang Fuk Court with a new beginning support grant worth HK$300,000 disbursed in two instalments: HK$150,000 at the end of December 2026, alongside the third instalment of the rental grant, and HK$150,000 at the end of June 2027 alongside the fourth instalment.

The grant will be provided to all flat owners, the government said.

If an owner has sold or is going to sell the flat title to the government, the grant will be disbursed to the person who was the owner before the transfer of title, it said.

A separate HK$200,000 grant will be provided to families of each deceased resident, in view of the public's desire to offer greater support and the fact that some of the deceased were non-flat owners, the government said.

It will be disbursed in one instalment at the end of December 2026.

The grants will be disbursed through the Social Welfare Department's "one social worker per household" mechanism, and flat owners and families of the deceased are not required to submit separate applications.

For families of deceased foreign domestic helpers, contact will be made through the relevant consulates, Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak said.

Warner Cheuk, Deputy Chief Secretary and convenor of the Steering Committee on the Support Fund, said the fund has, since its establishment, rolled out various support measures to assist residents who temporarily lost their home.

He said that as emergency and medium-term measures have been steadily implemented and the Special Sales Exercise is largely completed, flat owners and families of the deceased are progressing towards a new beginning.

"The Support Fund has decided to roll out two grants to assist the flat owners and families of the deceased in addressing their needs in this new stage of life, embarking on a new beginning, and moving forward from the tragic event," Cheuk said in the statement.

The two new measures involve a total of about HK$630 million.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: UK concert evacuated after unknown substance released
articles.excerpt: British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from a concert venue in Manchester, northern England, after the release of an…
articles.fullText:
British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from a concert venue in Manchester, northern England, after the release of an "unknown substance" required some in the crowd to be treated and one person to be taken to hospital.

Police declared a major incident late on Sunday after staff at the Co-op Live arena alerted them at 10 pm that people in the crowd had fallen ill during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver.

The ambulance service for the North West England area said it assessed more than 80 people for "eye and respiratory symptoms," while attendees referred to a "horrible smell" and people choking, the BBC reported.

Police said on Monday they had started an investigation to find out what the substance was and how it was released after the ambulance service earlier reported the substance was believed to be tear gas.

Tear gas is a chemical irritant that temporarily incapacitates people by burning their eyes, nose and throat.

In their statement, police advised anyone who notices side-effects or becomes ill to go to hospital.

"Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert," Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said in a statement on Monday.

Co-op Live said it was working closely with police to identify the cause of the incident.

The venue opened in 2024 and is located about 5 km away from the Manchester Arena in the centre of the city, where 22 people were killed in a suicide bombing at an Ariana Grande concert in 2017.

Toliver, who has been nominated for several Grammys this year, had been due to perform at London's O2 Arena on Monday, but the concert was postponed to December 15 as a result of Sunday's incident, the venue said in a statement. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: UK Grand Theft Auto VI hacker gets 7-year sentence
articles.excerpt: A UK court sentenced a British hacker to seven years in jail on Monday for a series of cyberattacks, including…
articles.fullText:
A UK court sentenced a British hacker to seven years in jail on Monday for a series of cyberattacks, including leaking footage from Grand Theft Auto VI years before the blockbuster game's release.

Having already served years in custody, Arion Kurtaj, aged 21, was entitled to walk free immediately, Judge Mark Turner said at London's Woolwich Crown Court.

Kurtaj, who is autistic, pleaded guilty last week to hacking major companies between 2021 and 2022, including GTA-maker Rockstar Games, mobile operator BT/EE, digital bank Revolut and ride-hailing giant Uber.

Turner described the offences as "sophisticated attacks upon big companies."

"Don't let this happen again," he added.

The judge said his sentencing decision required "balancing the seriousness of what you did with, on the other hand, your young age" and medical diagnoses.

Kurtaj was a teenager when he carried out the attacks as a key member of the so-called Lapsus$ hacking group.

He was initially charged over hacking BT/EE and placed in a hotel for his own protection from rival hackers in September 2022, according to the Crown Prosecution Service.

But from his hotel room, he went on to carry out cyberattacks on Revolut, Uber and Rockstar.

Using just a mobile phone, the hotel's wifi-connected TV and an Amazon Fire TV Stick, he broke into Rockstar systems and obtained 90 videos of the highly-anticipated GTA VI game.

He leaked the videos online under the username "TeaPotUberHacker," more than a year before the first official footage was released by Rockstar, causing a frenzy across the video game industry.

The hack disrupted the release strategy for the sixth instalment of the GTA franchise, which was finally released last week after a 13-year wait.

In 2023, a jury concluded that Kurtaj, whom psychiatrists at the time had deemed unfit to stand trial, was responsible for numerous computer misuse, fraud and blackmail offences.

Due to the severity of his autism, he was placed under a hospital order where he remained for two years before being found fit to stand trial, his lawyers said. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: USA to co-host 2031 Women's World Cup, UK to host 2035
articles.excerpt: A US-led joint bid was confirmed by Fifa on Monday as the host of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while…
articles.fullText:
A US-led joint bid was confirmed by Fifa on Monday as the host of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while the 2035 tournament will be hosted in the United Kingdom.

The winning bids were voted by acclamation after Fifa president Gianni Infantino confirmed the United States in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time.

The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035.

Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at Monday's meeting of Fifa's member associations.

"As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years."

The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final.

The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams.

The USA has hosted the Women's World Cup twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and is also the most successful nation in the tournament's history, having lifted the trophy four times.

No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Brentford sink Everton to climb in Premier League
articles.excerpt: Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday…
articles.fullText:
Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday.

Lewis-Potter's luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match.

Vitaly Janelt's stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday.

David Moyes's record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table.

A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford.

Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally.

The winger's first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself towards the ball.

Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin.

Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday's Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool.

Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago.

Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt's strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half.

The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time.

Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute.

Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils.

United sit second bottom of the table after a nine-game winless league run, plunging the English giants into danger of being relegated for the first time in 52 years. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Bangladesh garment workers say wage offer 'too low'
articles.excerpt: Bangladesh's garment factory owners offered workers on Monday far less than they have demanded in weeks of strikes and protests…
articles.fullText:
Bangladesh's garment factory owners offered workers on Monday far less than they have demanded in weeks of strikes and protests calling for a higher minimum wage, a representative said.

The South Asian nation, the world's second-biggest garment exporter behind China, has seen widespread protests since October by workers demanding higher pay.

Strikes have continued at several of the more than 4,000 factories in the country, with a trade body estimating hundreds of millions of dollars in losses and damages due to the prolonged disruption.

Workers say their pay has failed to keep pace with rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare. They are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (US$240), up from the current 12,500 taka.

Babul Akhter, the workers' representative on a wage board set up to resolve the crisis, said the latest offer was unacceptable.

"The factory owners' offer is too low, while they accuse us of making excessive demands," Akhter told reporters at a briefing after a marathon meeting.

"The offer... falls far short of what we have been demanding."

The board's chairman, Judge Syed Azad Subhani, said the proposed minimum wage was above 14,500 taka.

Akhter said the board would not disclose the exact offers to avoid "tension and confusion" as negotiations continue.

The factory owners' representative on the wage board, A B M Shamsuddin, said workers' demands were unrealistic given the state of the industry.

"A healthy duck can lay a golden egg every day, but can you expect the same from a sick duck?" Shamsuddin told reporters

In 2023, workers demanded a minimum wage of 23,000 taka, but agreed to 12,500 after negotiations.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association said on Sunday that protests had cost the industry an estimated US$428 million in losses, while orders worth US$254 million had shifted to other countries.

The garment industry, which supplies major international brands including Fruit of the Loom and Levi Strauss, earns around US$38 billion annually and accounts for four-fifths of Bangladesh's export earnings. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Ex-PMs stuck in the past over Brexit: Burnham
articles.excerpt: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham accused predecessors who have warned him against reigniting the Brexit debate of being "stuck in…
articles.fullText:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham accused predecessors who have warned him against reigniting the Brexit debate of being "stuck in the past", as he trumpeted his EU reset deal on Monday.

Burnham has in recent weeks smashed a general consensus that Britain's acrimonious departure from the European Union was done and dusted, floating the possibility that Britain could apply to rejoin.

Britain narrowly voted to leave the 27-member bloc in 2016. Now pro-Brexit voices are reorganising to prepare for likely looming battles over Britain's long-term relationship with the EU, as Burnham vows to pursue closer ties.

In recent days, former Conservative prime ministers Rishi Sunak, Theresa May, David Cameron and Boris Johnson have all urged Labour leader Burnham not to reopen old wounds.

"Those who say we shouldn't talk about Brexit risk leaving Britain stuck in the past with a substandard set of arrangements," Burnham told parliament.

"Instead, we are putting Britain back on a better path and bringing back the hope that has been missing for too long," he added in a speech about the UK-EU deals signed in Brussels last Friday.

Burnham and the EU's top officials sealed agreements to ease trade and youth mobility, although they kicked down the road tricky disagreements over British university fees for EU students.

The UK government argues the deals will eventually add £17 billion to Britain's economy per year, easing cost-of-living pressures and providing opportunities for young people.

They mean there is a "very real prospect that the next decade can be a much better one for Britain than the one we have just lived through," Burnham told MPs.

Earlier, Burnham told broadcasters that he "won't be listening to those voices who put us here in the first place."

"They're stuck in the past because they can't face up to the bad deal that they did," he said.

Sunak, premier from 2022 to 2024, told Sky News that restarting the "divisive" Brexit debate would become an "all-consuming" distraction for Burnham's government.

In an interview with the BBC, May – whose 2016 to 2019 tenure was dominated by her failure to pass a Brexit deal – urged Burnham to "accept Brexit and move on."

This echoed warnings from Cameron, who called the referendum and resigned following the result, and Johnson, who then took Britain out of the bloc in early 2020.

The comments evoked the so-called Brexit wars that dominated UK political discourse for years following the narrow vote.

Nigel Farage, the leader of the anti-EU Reform UK party, said on Monday that "going backwards into the EU's orbit would be a disaster for the very British businesses that are trying to compete and innovate."

Conservative opposition leader Kemi Badenoch meanwhile accused Burnham of "trying to take Britain back to 2015 instead of focusing on the future."

Burnham has previously said he would like to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime but has not taken a formal position since kick-starting a "national conversation" on Britain's future long-term relationship with the bloc.

He told parliament that British and EU negotiators would engage in an "informal exchange of ideas" about possible options, with the "results to be presented around the time of the next UK-EU summit," expected in 12 months.

Burnham has said the British public will be "the boss" over the future relationship, but has not said whether this means another referendum.

He has ruled out free movement or rejoining the single market or customs union during this parliament, which will end when he calls a general election, expected in 2029.

Several Labour MPs have praised Burnham for breaking the taboo over Brexit and have said he should put rejoining in the party's next manifesto, but the party is divided. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Trump 'secured deal for Huang's return to Nvidia'
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump said on Monday he secured a deal with the Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday he secured a deal with the Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, assuring them the Silicon Valley leader he called a "national treasure" would not pose a risk to US national security.

Trump said he had been in touch with the board since Huang stepped down November 12 following revelations about his extramarital affairs with subordinates and a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang – who's the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed.

Trump, who counts Jensen Huang as among his closest friends in Silicon Valley, had pushed for his reinstatement despite the revelations in an extraordinarily public intervention by a US president into a company's decision-making.

"The board decided to do what we wanted to do. And one of the things the board wanted to know is there a national security problem?" Trump said in an interview with CNBC after the board's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO was announced.

"And after a lot of research... we said, 'No, it's not a problem,'" Trump said in the interview. "We feel very strongly that he's in good shape, very good shape."

"I called him up and I said, I ask you to do one thing, Jensen: work hard," Trump told CNBC. "I didn't talk about other things because he understands that... I just said work hard because if you work hard, there's nobody that can capture what you've done."

Trump also expressed concern that China could poach Jensen Huang in the nearly hour-long CNBC interview, saying "we have to protect our geniuses."

"Jensen could take the next plane to China, and I guarantee you they would give him whatever he wanted," he said.

Trump would not say if he attended any Nvidia board meeting, but told CNBC he was represented there.

In a social media post earlier on Monday, Trump welcomed the board's decision and called Jensen Huang a "great patriot and a national treasure." He said US Attorney General Todd Blanche has confirmed that the federal government has no evidence that Jensen Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Asked what the CIA had told him about the issue, Trump said, "Let me just say, I have clearance. And If I didn't have clearance, I wouldn't have done the deal," he told CNBC.

Trump said Jensen Huang’s leadership at Nvidia was needed to ensure the continued success of the company, as well as the US economy.

Meanwhile, the United States on Monday added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist.

US companies cannot ship goods, software and technology to companies on the entity list without a license, which is likely to be denied. Firms on the list can find it harder to get access to US-origin spare parts, software updates or licenses for intellectual property.

Megaspeed did not immediately return a request for comment. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Wall Street rebounds as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
articles.excerpt: US stocks surged on Monday, led by a more than 6 percent jump in the Nasdaq as Nvidia's reinstatement of…
articles.fullText:
US stocks surged on Monday, led by a more than 6 percent jump in the Nasdaq as Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO drove investors back into AI-related shares after last week's rout.

Shares of Nvidia, cornerstone of the AI trade, ended 31.5 percent higher, their biggest daily percentage gain since May 9, 2003. Nvidia had announced Huang's resignation on November 12 after revelations of extramarital affairs.

US President Donald Trump said he secured a deal with Nvidia's board to bring back Huang as CEO. "I believe my intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back," Trump told CNBC.

The news helped Wall Street recover from last week's sharp selloff. On Friday, the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections as worries mounted about the AI trade.

The Nasdaq-100 added more than US$2 trillion in market value on Monday, while the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 registered their biggest daily percentage jumps since the market surged after Trump paused his "Liberation Day" tariff package in April 2025. The Cboe volatility index plunged.

"The thought had been, and it's being borne out today, that Jensen Huang is uniquely important to Nvidia and to the AI trade," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments.

Still, he said, "you have one issue that is resolved – and it's a biggie – but you still have to see how the rest of things play out."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,447.98 points, or 3 percent, to 49,595.31, the S&P 500 rose 326.78 points, or 4.7 percent, to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1,471.83 points, or 6.5 percent, to 24,089.56.

Before Monday, the Nasdaq had come close to entering a bear market as investors worried about the heavy borrowing underpinning AI investment and questioned whether the sector could deliver sufficient returns. Fears of political scrutiny also mounted after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.

Last week's sharp decline came even as Anthropic had a super-sized market debut and Nvidia posted strong quarterly earnings.

Other megacap stocks also rose. Amazon.com was up 3.5 percent, Meta was up 6.6 percent and Alphabet was up 6.3 percent.

Also climbing were neocloud and data-centre companies, whose shares sold off after Huang's abrupt exit at Nvidia. Shares of CoreWeave jumped 22.3 percent.

"We don't think the rebound has run its course, and at these levels, it's not too late to gradually add back technology exposure," said Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

Ahead this week is Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report, which could give clues about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Bougainville independence from PNG could change geopolitical landscape: experts
articles.excerpt: Papua New Guinea faces a crucial vote in parliament that would create another sovereign state in the Pacific.
articles.fullText:
PORT MORESBY, Papua New Guinea – As Papua New Guinea’s Parliament prepares to deliberate on granting independence to the autonomous region of Bougainville, experts told Radio Free Asia that the decision could alter the geopolitical landscape, where China and Western powers compete for diplomatic influence.
Bougainville gained autonomous status in 2005, giving it its own constitution, elected president and parliament, as well as broad powers over local governance, natural resources and public services.
In a landmark referendum held in 2019, voters in the autonomous region overwhelmingly backed independence from Papua New Guinea, or PNG. The vote was part of a peace agreement that ended a decade-long separatist conflict, but its outcome was nonbinding and requires a final decision by PNG’s Parliament.
PNG’s Parliament is expected to resume deliberations during its November budget session on whether to ratify the referendum result, a decision that could pave the way for Bougainville to become one of the world’s newest sovereign states, but Wally Hiambhon, a journalist-turned-media consultant in PNG, told RFA that the emergence of more small Pacific states could create new vulnerabilities amid growing competition between major powers.
A map showing the location of Bougainville within Papua New Guinea.
(RFA) “A fragmented Pacific with too many small states presents the potential for instability and conflict in an environment where there exists super-power rivalry and influence,” said Hiambhon. “We should tread with caution and responsibility on this one.”
Port Moresby’s recent warming relationship with Beijing is concerning, James Tanis, a former Bougainville president who participated in the peace negotiations, told RFA.
He took particular issue with the shutdown of Taiwan’s representative office in Port Moresby in November, and said that under its current status, Bougainville has no control over its own foreign relations.
“Only independence will help Bougainville to choose its own international friends,” he said.
An independent Bougainville would be able to pursue its own diplomatic relationships, although international recognition and admission to the United Nations would present additional challenges.
The people have spoken
For Margaret Edoni, a self-employed mother in PNG, the question of whether Bougainville should become an independent country has a straightforward answer: the people have already made their choice.
“Yes, I think PNG should give independence to Bougainville,” she told RFA. “In the 2019 referendum, 97.7% of Bougainvilleans voted for independence. And as a democratic state, PNG must respect the Bougainville people’s choice.”
Others in PNG have also voiced support for independence, arguing that the overwhelming vote leaves the national government with little justification for rejecting it. Some have criticized Port Moresby’s handling of the process, accusing it of poor planning and indecisiveness.
Bougainville Referendum Commission staff count votes prior to the referendum announcement in Bougainville on Dec. 11, 2019. Voters backing Bougainville's independence from Papua New Guinea have won a landslide referendum victory, according to results released on Dec. 11.
(Llane Munau/AFP) The current debate began in October after the government formally presented the referendum result and two supporting documents to Parliament in August. Prime Minister James Marape said lawmakers would return to the matter in November before a vote.
Under a parliamentary procedure adopted in June, ratification requires an absolute three-quarters majority, or 89 votes in the 118-member Parliament.
A troubled history
Bougainville, an island region east of mainland PNG and geographically close to the Solomon Islands, has a long history of separatist aspirations.
The dispute intensified in the late 1980s over the Panguna copper and gold mine, once among the world’s largest, as grievances over environmental destruction and the distribution of mining revenues fueled an armed rebellion.
The conflict between separatists and PNG security forces, compounded by internal fighting, killed thousands of people and devastated infrastructure before a peace process brought the fighting to an end.
The 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement provided for regional autonomy, weapons disposal and an eventual referendum on independence.
A voter from Selau is seen at Buka market, Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, Nov. 30, 2019.
(Bougainville Referendum Commission/Jeremy Miller/Handout via Reuters) Nearly 25 years later, the region is approaching a decisive stage in implementing that agreement.
Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama said on Nov. 13 that his government had fulfilled its obligations under the peace process and expected PNG to demonstrate the same commitment.
Bougainville’s leadership has proposed a transition to self-government by September 2027, followed by full independence in 2030.
But approval from Port Moresby remains uncertain.
Marape has emphasized that Parliament must consider both Bougainville’s aspirations and the implications for PNG’s national unity. His government has proposed a negotiated transition of up to 15 years if lawmakers endorse independence, potentially subject to economic and security conditions.
What if Parliament says no?
Tanis warned that rejecting independence could jeopardize decades of efforts to establish lasting peace.
“It is better to simply endorse and complete the process rather than not endorse and throw the process into the unknown,” he told RFA.
Tanis argued that the responsibility for securing the necessary parliamentary majority rested with Marape’s ruling Pangu Party and its coalition partners.
He also questioned what would follow a rejection, saying the agreements governing the peace process did not establish a clear pathway for implementing a negative vote.
Bougainville's President Ishmael Toroama speaks during the Papua New Guinea Investment Week conference in Sydney on Dec. 11, 2024.
(David Gray/AFP) Under the parliamentary procedure, a failed ratification vote would leave Bougainville’s existing autonomy arrangements in place, although the two governments could continue consultations.
Marape has suggested that a negative vote need not permanently settle the issue, leaving open the possibility of further negotiations.
But for supporters of independence, another delay could deepen frustration after years of waiting.
Mary Soondrawu, chairperson of PNG Trust Inc., an educational and advocacy organization, said the national government should respect the referendum outcome.
“The people have spoken and let their voice be heard,” she told RFA.
Can Bougainville survive alone?
Even if Parliament endorses independence, the region faces substantial economic challenges.
Bougainville relies heavily on financial transfers from PNG’s national government, raising questions about its ability to fund public services and maintain essential infrastructure as a sovereign country.
According to the Autonomous Bougainville Government, Bougainville’s internal annual revenue is 46.74 million kina (US$10.2 million), or just 5.5% of its budget for 2026 .
Delegations led by Chinese President Xi Jinping and Papua New Guinea’s Prime Minister James Marape attend a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China Nov. 17, 2026.
(Maxim Shemetov/Reuters) Marape has proposed that Bougainville demonstrate sufficient internal revenue to support at least 70% of its budget as part of a negotiated transition.
Mining could provide a potential source of revenue, although the legacy of Panguna remains contentious.
On Nov. 16, global mining group Rio Tinto announced a commitment of US$250 million over several years to a fund addressing environmental and human rights impacts associated with the former mine.
PNG Trust Inc.’s Soondrawu said independence should allow Bougainville to pursue accountability for environmental damage and make its own economic decisions.
Hiambhon warned that the economic realities of independence could prove more difficult than its supporters anticipate.
“My view is that whilst the majority of Bougainvilleans want independence, the reality of self-rule might be tougher than they reckon, particularly economic wellbeing,” he told RFA.
Edited by Taejun Kang and Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Fire services laws set for amendment
articles.excerpt: The Fire Services (Amendment) Bill 2026 and the Fixed Penalty (Fire Services) Bill will be published in the Government Gazette…
articles.fullText:
The Fire Services (Amendment) Bill 2026 and the Fixed Penalty (Fire Services) Bill will be published in the Government Gazette on Friday and introduced into the Legislative Council on December 2 for first and second readings, with the Government targeting completion of the legislative exercise within its current term.

The Security Bureau said today that the two bills will ensure that the existing fire safety legislative framework keeps pace with the times, and are designed to enhance public safety and regulatory coherence, boost enforcement effectiveness, and clarify industry accountability.

The bureau iterated that the Government attaches great importance to fire safety. Following the No. 5 alarm fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po in November 2025, the Government promptly established a "Task Force on Strengthening Fire Safety Governance", chaired by the Secretary for Security, to conduct a comprehensive review of the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95) and its subsidiary legislation, and to map out medium-to-long-term reform measures. The legislative review was highlighted as a priority reform item in the 2026 Policy Address.

The proposed legislative amendments encompass six pillars, namely strengthening the regulatory regime for fire service installations (FSIs) and equipment; introducing an FSI "responsible persons" regime; reforming the Registered Fire Service Installation Contractor registration and disciplinary regime; enhancing penalties and criminal accountability, introducing a fixed penalty regime and streamlining the fire hazard abatement workflow; and expanding the enforcement powers of the Fire Services Department in combatting illicit fuelling.

The bureau said it consulted the LegCo Panel on Security on the legislative amendment proposals on May 5, and that members were generally supportive. The Government then launched a one-month public consultation exercise on May 26.

Out of 506 valid submissions received, the bureau said 477 expressed support or made positive comments, reflecting that the proposals command wide support from the community.

articles.title: FS begins visit to Cambridge, UK
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan, leading a Hong Kong business and innovation and technology (I&T) delegation, began his visit to Cambridge…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan, leading a Hong Kong business and innovation and technology (I&T) delegation, began his visit to Cambridge in the UK yesterday.

Members of the delegation include Chairman of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) Frederick Ma and three Legislative Council (LegCo) members.

In the morning, Mr Chan met University of Cambridge Vice-Chancellor Deborah Prentice to discuss co-operation in scientific research, talent nurturing and the commercialisation of research outcomes. He briefed her on Hong Kong’s latest I&T progress and the Northern Metropolis University Town, inviting the university to expand research ties with local institutions.

Mr Chan then led the delegation to the UK-Hong Kong Innovation Dialogue – a roundtable co-organised by the HKTDC and the Cambridge Institute for Sustainability Leadership – for an in-depth exchange with local academics and representatives from think tanks, I&T firms and the investment sector.

Speaking at the roundtable, Mr Chan noted the strong foundation for UK-Hong Kong research collaboration, pointing out that eight UK universities, including Cambridge, have partnered with Hong Kong institutions to set up more than 10 joint laboratories under the InnoHK clusters. He added that Cambridge-headquartered biopharmaceutical firm AstraZeneca has also established a research and development (R&D) centre in Hong Kong.

Describing Hong Kong as an international financial centre and a bridge linking the Mainland with the world, Mr Chan noted that I&T is one of the four priority centres under Hong Kong’s first Five-Year Plan, which aims to boost original innovation and accelerate the city’s growth into an international I&T hub. He said Hong Kong and Cambridge can deepen ties across capital, connectivity and talent to jointly advance scientific research and commercialise outcomes.

On capital, Mr Chan said that Hong Kong provides technology firms with end-to-end financing from the laboratory to the public market, backed by private equity and venture capital funds managing about US$250 billion. He noted that the Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited has invested in more than 250 projects – attracting over eight dollars in market co-investment for every dollar spent – while over 90 pre-revenue biotech firms have raised more than 14 billion British pounds in Hong Kong since listing rules were relaxed in 2018.

On connectivity, he highlighted that the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), home to 88 million people, offers top innovation clusters and advanced manufacturing as a testing ground, production base and market for new technologies. He added that the Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone has started operating, with over 100 enterprises and institutions already moved in.

The financial chief noted that UK-approved drugs can apply for Hong Kong registration using that approval alongside local clinical trial data, and subsequently be used in designated GBA Mainland healthcare institutions under the Hong Kong & Macao Medicine & Equipment Connect policy, which had approved 79 drugs and 100 medical devices by the end of September. With many Mainland technology firms using Hong Kong as an international base, the city’s common law system and robust intellectual property protection also make it an ideal nexus for UK-China I&T collaboration, he added.

On talent, Mr Chan said Hong Kong boasts five universities in the world’s top 100 and continues to draw leading scientists, including two Nobel laureates in physics who joined the University of Hong Kong over the past year.

He invited UK research institutions and businesses to partner with delegation members, consider establishing offices and R&D bases in Hong Kong and tap the city’s capital market for fundraising. Given Cambridge’s research strengths and Hong Kong’s edge in commercialisation, financing and accessing Asian markets, he expressed hope that both sides would combine their advantages to bring research innovations to wider markets.

Following lunch at St John’s College with leaders and academics from various University of Cambridge colleges, Mr Chan and the delegation met Cambridge Enterprise, the university’s commercialisation arm. They discussed its experience in intellectual property commercialisation, start-up incubation and early-stage investment, while exploring collaboration opportunities with Hong Kong.

The delegation later visited AstraZeneca’s Discovery Centre in Cambridge, where management briefed them on advances in new drug R&D and artificial intelligence applications. Both sides discussed deepening co-operation to jointly develop innovative drugs and expand market reach using Hong Kong’s strengths as an international health and medical innovation hub, with Mr Chan welcoming AstraZeneca to further expand its local R&D operations.

articles.title: Hospital suspended from eHealth
articles.excerpt: The Health Bureau said today that it had suspended the eHealth registration of Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong (GHK) upon notification…
articles.fullText:
The Health Bureau said today that it had suspended the eHealth registration of Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong (GHK) upon notification by the hospital yesterday of unauthorised activity resulting in leakage of patients’ personal data.

GHK notified the bureau’s Electronic Health Record Office (eHRO) that on November 18 it discovered unauthorised activity involving the security infrastructure supporting its patient mobile application, My Gleneagles SmartHealth, resulting in unauthorised access to personal data, including that of certain patients.

The bureau said it is highly concerned about the incident and immediately suspended GHK's eHealth registration.

GHK indicated that it has engaged independent cybersecurity experts to conduct an investigation, as well as reporting the incident to the relevant law enforcement and regulatory authorities. It will also notify the affected patients.

The bureau stated GHK is a registered healthcare provider on eHealth, adding that the GHK mobile application concerned has no direct connection to the eHealth system.

The overall operation of eHealth has remained normal, and there is no evidence indicating that the eHealth system has been compromised or that any personal data within the system has been leaked.

The eHRO nevertheless decided to suspend GHK's eHealth registration, in view of its principles of prudence and risk management, and in order to safeguard the eHealth system's security and integrity.

The Government will examine the situation, looking in particular at potential risks to eHealth and any system security protection measures that can be adopted. It will also disseminate relevant security guidelines to registered healthcare providers on eHealth.

The Department of Health said it immediately sent staff to GHK to look into the incident after receiving the hospital's notification yesterday. It has asked the hospital to submit a detailed investigation report on the incident within four weeks.

It also urged GHK to notify all affected patients as soon as possible, and to take appropriate measures to ensure that the incident does not affect the hospital’s operations and clinical services.

articles.title: New grants rolled out for Tai Po fire
articles.excerpt: The Support Fund for Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po today rolled out two grants for affected flat owners and…
articles.fullText:
The Support Fund for Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po today rolled out two grants for affected flat owners and families of those who died in the fire to assist them in starting a new life.

The fund will provide owners of each flat with a new beginning support grant of $300,000, to be disbursed in two installments.

The first installment of $150,000 will be disbursed at the end of December, alongside the third rental grant payout, whereas the second tranche of $150,000 will be issued at the end of June 2027, alongside the fourth rental grant installment.

If a flat owner has sold or is going to sell their flat title to the Government, the grant will be disbursed to the person who owned the property prior to the transfer.

In view of the public's desire to offer greater support to bereaved families, and given that some of the deceased were not flat owners, the fund will provide a separate new beginning support grant for them.

This grant of $200,000 will be provided for each deceased person and disbursed in a single lump sum at the end of December.

Convenor of the Steering Committee on the Support Fund for Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po and Deputy Chief Secretary Cheuk Wing-hing said those affected are progressing towards a new beginning as various emergency and medium-term support measures have been steadily implemented, and the Special Sales Exercise is largely completed.

“Therefore, pursuant to the instruction of the Chief Executive, the support fund has decided to roll out two grants to assist the flat owners and families of the deceased in addressing their needs in this new stage of life, embarking on a new beginning, and moving forward from the tragic event," he said.

articles.title: Tiangong exhibit opens
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Space Museum will launch a free exhibition from tomorrow to July 19 next year to showcase astronauts’…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Space Museum will launch a free exhibition from tomorrow to July 19 next year to showcase astronauts’ lives aboard the Tiangong Space Station and the journey of the city's first payload specialist, Lai Ka-ying.

Titled "Reaching for the Cosmos: Astronauts' Log Aboard Tiangong", the exhibition will take visitors through Ms Lai’s journey from the ignition of the Long March rocket and the liftoff of the Shenzhou spacecraft to boarding the Tiangong Space Station.

In addition to the work and lives of the country's astronauts on the space station, the exhibition will also introduce the latest technologies that China has applied aboard it, as well as Hong Kong’s participation and contributions.

Through interactive exhibits and models, visitors can learn about the Long March-2F rocket, the Shenzhou spacecraft, and the Tiangong Space Station. A full-scale model of the Multi-Spectral Imaging Carbon Observatory (MUSICO) – the first local scientific payload aboard the Tiangong Space Station – will also be displayed.

Together with interactive games and multimedia programmes, the exhibition introduces the functions of MUSICO and Tiangong's robotic arms, allowing visitors to try operating a robotic arm to move an object.

The exhibition will also showcase the expertise and responsibilities of spacecraft pilots, spaceflight engineers, and payload specialists in Shenzhou manned spaceflight missions, as well as the physical changes astronauts experience in space, how they cope with the unique challenges of living there, and the onboard dining and sleeping area equipment.

Hong Kong has long contributed to the country's aerospace programmes, drawing on its strengths in scientific research, innovation and technology to support various space missions.

The exhibition outlines the city's participation in manned spaceflight projects and educational programmes, encouraging young people to take an active part in space-related initiatives.

articles.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
articles.excerpt: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, less than two weeks after its co-founder resigned. The Nvidia board…
articles.fullText:
Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, less than two weeks after its co-founder resigned.

The Nvidia board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his "candour and ability to lead," the company said in a statement.

"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

Huang said he was "honoured" to return to the company, was grateful for the "extraordinary support" he received since his resignation and that he "can't wait to get back to work".

“I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang’s statement said. “Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

US President Donald Trump welcomed his reinstatement, calling it the correct decision, and added that it poses no threat to American national security.

"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Trump said in a social media post.

The board decision came three days after Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Huang back, calling him "one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world" and saying he would "love to see Jensen be given a second chance".

The company said Colette Kress would continue as chief financial officer.

Nvidia shares surged as much as 36 percent before closing 31 percent higher, driving a broad rally across chip-related and technology stocks on Wall Street.

Huang had resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, and Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said last week that the company would not rehire him despite the growing campaign for his return.

The board's decision to bring Huang back highlights his deep influence over Nvidia and raises questions about how dependent one of the world's most valuable companies remains on its co-founder. (Agencies)
