articles.title: Ukraine attacks Russian warship in Libya
articles.excerpt: Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, the day after a drone…
articles.fullText:
Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, the day after a drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

Libya's eastern-based government said the corvette, the Merkury, had been docked at the Benghazi naval base.

Zelensky published videos on Monday from Ukraine's SBU security service that he said showed the attack, and another drone off Libya hitting the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which he said Moscow had used to transport weapons.

The footage, verified by Reuters, showed fire erupting and smoke billowing from the ships.

Ukraine's SBU security service said the drones used in Sunday's attack had been launched from a "mother ship" in the region.

While Russia and Ukraine have repeatedly attacked each other's military and commercial shipping in the Black Sea, attacks elsewhere have been rarer.

The SBU said the operation showed that the Russian navy had "no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea".

Zelensky's post on Telegram was the first official acknowledgement that Ukraine has carried out an attack in Libya. He said Russia had tried, but failed, to counter the attack on the corvette.

He said a Russian Ka-27 combat helicopter had also been destroyed, adding: "We continue operations in designated waters."

Russia's Defence Ministry did not immediately comment.

After a civil war, eastern Libya is controlled by military commander Khalifa Haftar, whose Libyan National Army has ties with Russia, while the west is controlled by an internationally recognised Government of National Unity based in Tripoli.

The Institute for the Study of War said the Merkury had stopped over for several days, under a cooperation agreement, to refuel and resupply as it escorted Russian cargo ships that can carry military supplies en route to Russia.

Osama Hamad, prime minister of Libya's eastern-based government, said he had asked the UN to investigate "suspicions that the boats had been launched from western Libya" and to verify the presence of Ukrainian military experts there.

No comment was immediately available from the Tripoli government.

Russia's Transport Ministry said in March that Ukrainian naval drones launched from Libya had attacked the Arctic Metagaz, which was carrying liquefied natural gas from Murmansk. Libya's maritime agency said the vessel had sunk between Libya and Malta after catching fire. Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for that attack.

On Saturday, a drone attack set fire to another Russian cargo ship, the Sparta II, operated by the Russian defence logistics firm Oboronlogistika, in international waters in the Gulf of Finland.

The Finnish military said it was likely to have been carried out by Ukraine, although Kyiv did not immediately comment.

All 16 crew were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship, one slightly injured.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov answered a question about the attack by saying there was a "dangerous trend of increasing terrorist activity" in the Baltic Sea. He said Moscow hoped adjoining states would warn Kyiv off such operations.

Russian, Estonian and Finnish vessels fought the fire after the Sparta II drifted into Finnish waters, and a Russian ship began towing it away on Sunday.

US-backed talks between Russia and Ukraine resumed this month after a nine-month hiatus in an effort to end the war, Europe's biggest since World War Two, albeit with little result so far.

Mykola Bielieskov of the National Institute for Strategic Studies in Kyiv said Ukraine was looking to strengthen its position with "horizontal escalation".

"Since neither side is able to compel the other to accept terms of settlement through the battlefield only, both try to find new ways to pressure each other," he said. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Govt to speed up building maintenance reforms: CE
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee has ordered all government bureaux and departments to accelerate sweeping reforms to the building maintenance and…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee has ordered all government bureaux and departments to accelerate sweeping reforms to the building maintenance and renovation regime to prevent a repeat of the tragedy at Wang Fuk Court.

The directives came as Lee chaired a meeting on Monday to receive briefings from officials on the government’s progress in implementing systemic reforms and taking forward the recommendations of the independent committee on the inferno that killed 168 people.

The government released the committee’s report last month and announced reforms in six areas. A steering committee led by Chief Secretary Eric Chan held its first meeting last week.

Officials said 29 recommendations have been fully implemented, while the rest are being taken forward with implementation timetables and, in some cases, industry consultation.

Lee instructed officials to submit amendments to six pieces of legislation to the Legislative Council as soon as possible.

The Fire Services Ordinance amendment bill will be introduced for first and second reading next month, while proposed changes to the Building Management Ordinance proposals were sent to Legco earlier this month, with details being finalised and the bill to be submitted as soon as possible.

Buildings Ordinance amendments will go to the Legco Panel on Development on November 24, with a target of submitting the bill early next year.

Amendments to the Competition Ordinance, Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance and Independent Commission Against Corruption Ordinance will be introduced early next year to combat bid-rigging and other serious anti-competitive conduct in building maintenance.

Meanwhile, the Building Maintenance Support and Services Council – which aims to assist homeowners to manage related works – will be established within this year and begin compiling three "pre-qualified lists" next month.

An expert panel on major building maintenance will also be set up by the Development Bureau this month.

On enforcement, a joint task force against bid-rigging in building maintenance and renovation projects has arrested 163 people in two operations, involving over HK$230 million.

Lee said the reforms must be implemented rigorously and in full.

"We must all learn from the lesson, and earnestly implement reform measures to prevent such tragedies from recurring, and continue to provide full support to the affected residents to help them begin their new lives as soon as possible," he said in a statement.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Google AI smartwatch could flag high blood pressure
articles.excerpt: Google's AI used smartwatch sensors to spot hypertension without a blood pressure cuff, but the Nature study found it missed…
articles.fullText:
When was the last time you checked your blood pressure? If you're like a lot of people, it probably happened during your last doctor's appointment. And if you feel perfectly healthy , you may not give it another thought. That's what makes high blood pressure so concerning. You can have it for years without noticing anything wrong.
Now, Google researchers are exploring a way to uncover that hidden danger using something many of us already wear on our wrists. In a new study recently published in Nature, researchers demonstrated an artificial intelligence system that can identify signs of hypertension using standard smartwatch sensors. It works in the background without requiring calibration with a traditional blood pressure cuff.
The technology uses sensors that already exist in consumer smartwatches. That could make early detection much more accessible. However, the research also reveals a limitation that anyone relying on a smartwatch for health information should understand.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
SMARTWATCH AFIB ALERT SENDS DAD TO ER BEFORE HEART SURGERY
Your smartwatch already knows quite a bit about your body. It can track your heart rate throughout the day. Depending on the model, it may also detect irregular heart rhythms.
Google's new AI takes the information collected by those sensors and looks for signs of something harder to detect: ongoing high blood pressure. According to Google Research , the system analyzes two types of sensor data.
The first sensor uses light to detect changes in blood volume beneath your skin. It's the same basic technology many watches use to monitor your pulse. The second sensor measures movement. Researchers found that it can also capture incredibly small vibrations caused by your heart pumping blood. You wouldn't notice those vibrations. However, the AI can analyze them alongside your pulse patterns to look for signs associated with hypertension.
The system collects information over multiple days. It then combines those patterns with your height to estimate the likelihood of sustained high blood pressure. Unlike a traditional monitor, the smartwatch doesn't produce a reading such as 120 over 80. Instead, it looks for signs that your blood pressure may be consistently elevated. What's interesting is that you wouldn't have to do anything differently. You could go about your day while your smartwatch quietly looks for potential warning signs.
Google worked with researchers from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School to develop and test the system. First, researchers trained the underlying AI using nearly 500,000 hours of smartwatch sensor data collected from 2,109 consenting participants. They then evaluated the hypertension detection system in a clinical study involving 196 participants across five U.S. locations. None of those participants had known cardiovascular disease or were taking blood pressure medication.
During the study, participants wore a consumer smartwatch for seven days. Researchers compared the AI's findings with results from 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring. That medical test uses a cuff to measure blood pressure repeatedly throughout the day and night. Doctors use it to help confirm hypertension.
During initial screening, the results showed:
For comparison, initial blood pressure screenings performed in medical offices identified 55.3% of participants with hypertension in the study. That's an encouraging result. However, the difference between the smartwatch and office screening was not statistically significant, according to a Nature Portfolio summary of the findings. There's another number worth paying attention to.
That's a number worth paying attention to. After all, we're talking about a condition that can lead to a heart attack or stroke , often without any warning signs.
Researchers also looked at a smaller group of 48 people who had elevated blood pressure readings during their initial doctor's visit. In that group, the AI correctly identified 78.4% of those with ongoing hypertension. It also correctly ruled out the condition in 90.9% of those who didn't have it. Those results are encouraging, but there's still work to do. Google needs to test the technology on more people before we can know how reliably it can detect high blood pressure.
MICROSOFT AI BEATS DOCTORS IN SIMULATED DIAGNOSIS TEST
Here's where things get interesting for people who already own a Google smartwatch. Google introduced its Health Guardian features in September 2026. Among them is a blood pressure trends feature available through the Google Health app.
According to Google's September announcement, blood pressure trends are available at no additional subscription cost on eligible Pixel Watch 3, Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 devices . Availability depends on your region.
The feature analyzes pulse and movement patterns over time. Then, it provides a monthly assessment of whether your blood pressure trend appears high. Google says these existing Health Guardian capabilities are informed by clinical research, including work connected to its newly published findings. However, there's an important difference between the experimental system described in Nature and the feature available on your watch today.
The existing Pixel Watch feature is intended for general wellness. Google specifically says it cannot diagnose hypertension or serve as a medical screening tool. It also cannot tell you your actual systolic or diastolic blood pressure numbers. According to Google's support documentation, the feature provides a monthly trend assessment such as "High" or "Not high."
And a "Not high" result doesn't guarantee your blood pressure is normal. Google also warns users against relying on these estimates to change medications or treatment plans. Meanwhile, the newly published research remains exploratory. Google has not announced that the experimental hypertension screening system will become a commercial diagnostic feature.
Google has some competition in this area. Apple has already introduced FDA-cleared hypertension notifications for compatible Apple Watch models. As we previously reported in Apple Watch gets FDA-approved hypertension alerts , the feature looks for patterns associated with chronic high blood pressure. It uses information gathered by the watch's optical heart sensor over 30-day periods.
The feature supports Apple Watch Series 9 and later models, along with Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models, subject to software and regional availability. If the watch detects concerning patterns, it can notify you. However, Apple also makes clear that the feature cannot diagnose hypertension. And it may miss cases. Apple recommends checking your blood pressure with a traditional cuff and discussing the results with a healthcare professional if you receive an alert.
So, while Apple and Google are approaching this technology differently, the current guidance remains clear. A smartwatch alert can give you useful information, but you still need an accurate blood pressure measurement.
High blood pressure has earned the nickname "silent killer" for a reason. According to the World Health Organization, more than one billion adults worldwide live with hypertension. Many have no idea they have it.
Meanwhile, untreated high blood pressure can damage blood vessels and increase the risk of a heart attack or stroke. Younger adults can be particularly vulnerable to missed diagnoses because they may feel healthy and see little reason to get checked. Now, consider what could happen if a smartwatch noticed concerning patterns before someone developed symptoms.
That person might decide to schedule an appointment and have their blood pressure checked. If doctors confirm hypertension, earlier treatment could help reduce the risk of complications. Of course, researchers still need to determine whether smartwatch-based screening actually improves diagnosis rates and long-term health outcomes.
COULD A PAINT-ON ELECTRONIC TATTOO SPOT HEART ATTACKS?
If your smartwatch warns you about possible high blood pressure, don't ignore it. But don't assume the watch has diagnosed you, either. The next step is to check your blood pressure using a validated upper-arm cuff.
The American Heart Association recommends automatic upper-arm monitors for home measurements because they provide more reliable readings than typical wrist or finger monitors. If you're using Google's blood pressure trends feature and receive a "High" result, Google recommends checking your blood pressure twice a day for seven days and sharing those readings with your doctor.
Make sure you follow your monitor's instructions and use the correct cuff size. Also, keep an eye on how you're feeling. If you experience emergency warning signs such as chest pain or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention rather than waiting for another smartwatch assessment.
And remember, even if your watch never sends an alert, you should continue getting your blood pressure checked. For another way to track your readings, see our article on how to monitor blood pressure with your Apple Watch using a compatible blood pressure monitor.
One of my biggest questions about this technology comes down to how much confidence people will place in the results. Let's say your smartwatch tells you everything looks normal. Would you still bother checking your blood pressure? That's where the research raises an important concern.
In Google's initial screening study, the AI missed a meaningful number of people who actually had hypertension. And while the results compared favorably with initial office screening, the study was relatively small. Researchers will need more evidence before the technology can become a dependable part of routine medical screening.
Google's findings suggest that everyday wearables could eventually help identify people who might otherwise go undiagnosed. For now, though, a reliable blood pressure cuff and a conversation with your doctor remain essential.
I like where Google is going with this. Most of us probably don't think about our blood pressure until we're sitting in a doctor's office with a cuff around our arm. So the idea that a smartwatch could spot a potential problem before we even know something's wrong is pretty exciting. But there's one number in this study that concerns me. The AI missed roughly one in three people who actually had high blood pressure. That's a lot, especially when you consider the serious health risks involved. I think this technology has tremendous potential, and I'm looking forward to seeing how Google improves it. But for now, I wouldn't rely on my smartwatch to tell me whether my blood pressure is normal. I'd still want to check it with a traditional cuff.
Would you trust your smartwatch to warn you about high blood pressure? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

articles.title: FBI warns AI hackers can breach systems in under 3 hours
articles.excerpt: The FBI warns the ARTEX AI hacking tool can give criminals privileged access in under three hours, targeting Microsoft 365…
articles.fullText:
Your bank could spend millions protecting its computer systems. Your employer might have an entire cybersecurity team watching for suspicious activity . Yet hackers now have an AI-powered tool that can help them break into some organizations in less than three hours.
The FBI is warning that criminals are using the ARTEX AI hacking tool to automate cyberattacks against businesses around the world. Some attacks have moved from initial targeting to powerful administrator-level access in under three hours. That leaves companies very little time to recognize an attack and stop it.
If hackers reach a business that stores your personal information, you could end up dealing with the consequences. Here's how ARTEX works, why the FBI is concerned and what you can do to protect yourself.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
AI-POWERED CYBERATTACKS FUEL 'BLACK OCTOBER' FEARS
ARTEX started as a legitimate penetration testing framework. Cybersecurity professionals use these tools to find weaknesses in computer systems before criminals discover them. However, hackers have found ways to turn ARTEX against organizations without permission. The framework uses artificial intelligence to handle tasks that previously required significant hacking expertise. It can search for security weaknesses and attempt to exploit them. Once inside a system, ARTEX can work toward gaining higher levels of access and extracting sensitive information. What makes ARTEX particularly concerning is its ability to operate with limited human involvement. Attackers can give the software instructions, then let AI agents carry out much of the work automatically.
ARTEX also connects to external AI models , including OpenAI's GPT and Anthropic's Claude. It supports DeepSeek and several other models. These integrations allow the framework to process instructions and automate complicated hacking operations. Their availability does not mean the AI companies are directing the attacks. According to the FBI, the technology allows criminals with relatively little technical knowledge to launch sophisticated attacks against multiple organizations simultaneously.
In a November 13, 2026, security advisory, the FBI warned that criminals have used ARTEX in cyberattacks since at least August 2026. The agency identified campaigns targeting financial institutions and healthcare organizations. Government agencies and technology companies have also appeared among the targets. The speed of these attacks is especially troubling. According to the FBI, some intrusions progressed from initial targeting to privileged access in less than three hours. That means hackers obtained powerful permissions that could allow them to make changes inside compromised systems.
ARTEX can also identify weaknesses in systems that companies sometimes overlook. These include employee portals and older business applications. Criminals may exploit vulnerable third-party connections to reach organizations with stronger security. Although automated attacks can trigger security alerts, their speed creates another challenge. A company's security team might detect suspicious activity only after criminals have already gained access.
One of the clearest examples involves Microsoft 365, the service millions of employees rely on for work email and company files. In October 2026, hackers exploited compromised application credentials associated with ConnectWise Cloud Backup. The service, formerly known as SkyKick Cloud Backup, helps businesses back up Microsoft 365 information. Here's why that attack is so concerning. The compromised applications already had permission to access customer environments. Hackers took advantage of those existing permissions to authenticate without needing an employee to sign in. In an October 21 investigation, Microsoft attributed the campaign to a China-state-aligned hacking group it tracks as Storm-0940.
The group used ARTEX to speed up its operations and attempt access to more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 customer environments. Cybersecurity company Huntress reported unauthorized sign-ins across at least 162 customer environments during its initial investigation. However, the number of environments targeted does not represent the number where criminals stole information. Microsoft specifically warned that successful authentication does not automatically mean customer data was accessed or taken. The attack also did not result from a vulnerability in Microsoft's own systems or services. Hackers exploited permissions associated with a trusted third-party application. For businesses, that's a serious concern. Employees could have strong passwords and multifactor authentication enabled, yet criminals might still gain access through a compromised application the company already trusts.
The Microsoft 365 incident represents only part of the FBI's warning. In South Korea, hackers used ARTEX in attacks against financial institutions. Those attacks exposed personal information belonging to approximately 67,000 people, according to the FBI.
In a separate investigation, South Korean authorities arrested seven suspects connected to attacks against more than 90 organizations. Police said the group stole approximately 8.2 million data records, with ARTEX reportedly used in many of the attacks. Researchers have also identified a separate international cyberespionage campaign.
Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike reported that a China-linked hacking group known as Vapor Panda used ARTEX in attacks targeting more than 200 organizations across 14 countries. The campaign compromised at least nine organizations. The AI agents helped criminals identify vulnerabilities and obtain credentials. When one attack method failed, the software could attempt another approach. These incidents show how quickly AI-assisted hacking has expanded from individual targets to coordinated attacks against organizations around the world.
You probably have never heard of ARTEX before now. But the businesses you depend on could become targets. Think about the information your employer keeps on file. It may include your Social Security number and banking details for direct deposit. Your healthcare provider holds sensitive medical information, while financial institutions maintain records connected to your identity. If criminals steal information from those organizations, they could use it to attempt identity theft or target you with convincing scams. A hacker who obtains your email address and details about your employer could create a phishing message that looks legitimate. A message mentioning a company you actually do business with may be harder to recognize as fraudulent.
There's another concern. Your personal information could be exposed through a company you barely remember giving it to. The FBI has not warned that ARTEX automatically compromises personal phones or home computers. Its advisory focuses on attacks against organizations and the systems they operate. Still, you don't have to be the direct target of a cyberattack to feel its effects.
NEW AI MALWARE RANKS VICTIMS BY HOW MUCH THEY'RE WORTH
The original ARTEX developer released the framework publicly in July 2026. After reports emerged that criminals were abusing it, the developer removed the original GitHub repository on October 8. However, the software remains available through archived copies and modified versions. The FBI also identified a commercial version called ARTEX PRO. As of early November, researchers had identified more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles. That figure refers to accessible framework interfaces, rather than 1,600 confirmed criminal operations. Removing the original project did little to eliminate copies already circulating online.
While companies are responsible for securing their systems, you can still take steps to protect your personal information and limit the damage if a business you trust gets hacked.
If criminals steal login credentials from one organization, they may test those credentials against other accounts. Reusing passwords makes that easier. Use a strong, unique password for every important account. A reputable password manager can generate secure passwords and store them for you. Start with your primary email account because criminals who gain access to it may be able to reset passwords for other services.
Multifactor authentication adds another security check when someone tries to sign in to your account. Enable it for your email and financial services whenever available. Choose a passkey or authenticator app when supported. Passkeys can provide stronger protection against phishing than traditional passwords. Keep in mind that these protections cannot prevent every attack. The ConnectWise incident involved compromised application credentials rather than someone entering an employee's password.
You may have granted third-party applications permission to access your Google or Microsoft account without thinking much about it. Review those connections periodically. Remove permissions for unfamiliar services or applications you no longer need. For personal Microsoft accounts, visit account.microsoft.com. For Google accounts, review your connected apps through myaccount.google.com. Look for unfamiliar sign-ins while you're there. If something seems suspicious, secure the account and revoke any sessions you don't recognize. For work accounts, contact your IT department before changing business application permissions.
Cybercriminals often use major security incidents to create convincing phishing messages. You might receive an email claiming your bank was hacked and asking you to verify your password. Another message could direct you to a fake account recovery page. Avoid clicking unexpected links or opening unfamiliar attachments. Instead, visit the company's official website or open its app directly to check for alerts. Never share verification codes with someone who contacts you unexpectedly, even if the person claims to work for your bank.
Install security updates on your computer and phone. These updates frequently address vulnerabilities criminals could exploit. Strong antivirus software with real-time protection can also help identify malicious downloads and suspicious programs. Some security tools offer additional protection against phishing websites. However, antivirus software on your personal computer cannot prevent criminals from compromising a company's cloud systems. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com.
Check your financial accounts regularly and enable transaction alerts. These notifications can help you spot unauthorized activity quickly. Review your credit reports for unfamiliar accounts or credit inquiries. You can request free reports through AnnualCreditReport.com. If your Social Security number has been exposed, consider freezing your credit with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A credit freeze is free and can make it harder for criminals to open new credit accounts using your identity. A freeze will not prevent fraud involving accounts that are already open, so continue monitoring those accounts.
VISA, MASTERCARD AND JPMORGAN CUSTOMER DATA LEAKED
If a company notifies you about a breach, find out exactly what information was compromised. Then take action based on the type of data involved.
You can also report suspected internet crime to the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center at ic3.gov/.
A backup service is supposed to help protect a company's information. In the ConnectWise attack, hackers abused that trusted connection to gain access to customer systems. That's especially concerning because employees could have followed every security recommendation and still been exposed through a service their company depended on. The speed of these AI-powered attacks also worries me. Three hours gives security teams very little time to stop criminals who know exactly where they're going. I think companies need to take a much harder look at the outside applications they trust and how quickly they can detect unauthorized access. For you, the best approach is to secure your own accounts and pay attention when a company reports a breach. You shouldn't have to become a cybersecurity expert to feel confident that businesses are protecting your information.
If AI-powered hackers can gain privileged access to company systems in less than three hours, do you still trust businesses to protect your personal information, or should companies face tougher consequences when that information gets exposed? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

articles.title: Mortgage Corp deepens Asian infrastructure bank bond
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) have signed a letter of intent that…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) have signed a letter of intent that sets out a framework for cooperation with the common goal of mobilising private capital into the infrastructure sector.

Under the letter of intent signed on November 20, the two sides intend to strengthen cooperation.

These include identifying and exploring potential co-financing opportunities in sustainable infrastructure, integrating relevant climate change strategy into infrastructure financing, developing talent for sustainable infrastructure finance, exchanging experience on digital tools, and deepening collaboration on infrastructure loan-backed securities (ILBS) issuances.

The HKMC said that over the past three years, AIIB has continued to support its ILBS issuances as an anchor investor through its US$300 million Project Ocean investment programme.

The corporation said it has been regularly issuing ILBS under its Bauhinia brand name for the past three years, in line with its mandate to develop Hong Kong's local debt capital market, with the long-term goal of promoting ILBS as a standalone asset class and strengthening the city's position as an infrastructure financing hub.

The issuances offer professional investors exposure to a diversified portfolio of projects and infrastructure debts across multiple geographies and industry sectors, it said.

It said the infrastructure bank's involvement, given its status as a multilateral development bank, has strengthened investor confidence, furthering growth of the investor base and increasing private capital mobilisation.

"With the significant growth of HKMC's infrastructure financing and securitisation platform in the past few years, we hope to reinforce our collaboration with our network of financial institutions, commercial banks, and multilateral development banks," said corporation chief executive Colin Pou.

"Further advancing our partnership with AIIB will bring further opportunities to develop our business and promote the development of Hong Kong as an infrastructure financing hub."

For her part, Lim Kim See, a chief investment officer at AIIB, said the bank is delighted to broaden its engagement with the HKMC.

"We look forward to leveraging the expertise of both parties in infrastructure financing and supporting the continued development of ILBS, which together would mobilise private capital into emerging market infrastructure," she said.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HK slips as mainland, Kospi diverge amid stocks push
articles.excerpt: Mainland stocks rose as other Asian stock markets struggled to recover on Monday from last week's sell-off, with tech firms…
articles.fullText:
Mainland stocks rose as other Asian stock markets struggled to recover on Monday from last week's sell-off, with tech firms again in the firing line as investors tracked an eye-watering rout on Wall Street.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 27 points, or 0.1 percent, down at 22,383 turnover on HK$253.09 billion.

The tech index inched down three points, or 0.1 percent, to 3,508 while the China enterprises index fell 26 points, or 0.3 percent, to 7,527.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index inched up five points, or 0.15 percent, to close at 3,538 on turnover of 738.5 billion yuan.

The Shenzhen Component Index rose 197 points, or 1.93 percent, to 10,454 on turnover of 814.38 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index spiked up 68 points, or 3.08 percent, to 2,280 on turnover of 400.62 billion yuan.

In Seoul, the Kospi dived 161 points, or 3.31 percent, to 4,708 as a government pledge to deploy market stabilisation funds failed to ease concerns over the AI trade and a broader technology selloff that saw falls of 3.06 percent for chipmaker Samsung Electronics and 2.52 percent for its peer SK Hynix.

A healthy bounce in US futures was unable to inspire buying amid fears over the AI trade, the prospect of more Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and tighter regulation under a Democrat-led Congress.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix "are not peripheral players in the AI boom but two of its most important semiconductor suppliers", said SPI Asset Management's Stephen Innes.

"Their continued weakness suggests investors are still more interested in reducing exposure than celebrating a few hours of improved sentiment in US futures."

The losses have led authorities in some countries to introduce measures aimed at minimising the negative impact.

China has made it easier to borrow money to buy stocks while South Korea is eyeing a stabilisation fund not used since the global financial crisis.

Meanwhile, the VIX Index – which is seen as the market's fear gauge – spiked to its highest level since April last year, when US President Donald Trump unveiled his wide-ranging tariff bazooka.

Traders have also been spooked by the US Commerce Department's move to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to access Nvidia's powerful AI chips remotely.

Fiona Cincotta at Forex.com said "nerves have been showing in the AI trade, amid increased scrutiny over AI capital expenditure, the scale of investment, the returns on those investments and when they might materialise".

"Furthermore, the Democrats taking control of Congress, which is expected to slow the AI buildout, combined with expectations of higher rates for longer, are fuelling concerns about the sector." (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China says global green transition is 'irreversible'
articles.excerpt: China on Monday said the failure of a United Nations climate conference to produce a deal following a row over…
articles.fullText:
China on Monday said the failure of a United Nations climate conference to produce a deal following a row over fossil fuels was disappointing but that the green transition is "irreversible".

"We express our disappointment over this, while maintaining that confidence in the multilateral process should not be lost as a result," Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular news briefing.

"China wishes to emphasise that tackling climate change is a shared endeavour for all humanity. The trend of global transition to green energy low carbon is irreversible.

"China has been committed to safeguarding multilateralism, advancing international cooperation, and promoting green transition.

"China will continue to act responsibly and work with all parties to cope with challenges, overcome difficulties and promote the green and low-carbon transition and sustainable development worldwide."

For the first time since the 2009 meeting in Copenhagen, the COP climate conference in Türkiye could not reach a final agreement from its talks after the European Union and others rejected a final deal that did not include any mention of fossil fuels' role in global warming because of pressure from Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing nations. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Domestically-built cruise ship in Kai Tak maiden call
articles.excerpt: The second China-built large cruise ship, the Adora Flora City, arrived at Kai Tak Cruise Terminal on Monday morning on…
articles.fullText:
The second China-built large cruise ship, the Adora Flora City, arrived at Kai Tak Cruise Terminal on Monday morning on its maiden commercial voyage carrying more than 3,800 passengers.

The ship set sail from the Nansha International Cruise Home Port in Guangzhou for a six-day, five-night journey that will also take it to Hue in Vietnam.

The vessel is 341 metres long and has 2,130 cabins, with capacity for up to 5,232 passengers.

Compared with the first China-built large cruise ship, the Adora Magic City, the new vessel's hull has been lengthened by 17.4 metres, with more than 3,000 square metres of additional public space.

It also features a larger atrium, an upgraded water park and more passenger-friendly services.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Carolina in mind as Democrats' edge hits 258 in House
articles.excerpt: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard…
articles.fullText:
Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media have projected.

The latest win came after the party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard's win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress' 435-member House, with four more seats yet to be declared.

The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

"House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM," House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X.

Sunday's result came after Foxx requested a recount.

Hubbard said on Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who "graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".

"Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices," he added on X.

The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump's agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency.

The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump's war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'RMB primed to be internationally attractive currency'
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui said the internationalisation of the renminbi was not confined to payments…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui said the internationalisation of the renminbi was not confined to payments and settlement – it's about making it a currency with international appeal for investment and asset allocation.

He made the remarks as the first exchange-traded fund (ETF) tracking offshore renminbi bonds was listed on Monday.

Speaking at the listing ceremony, Hui said the fund would provide investors with an efficient and convenient tool.

It would not only meet global investors’ growing demands for diversified allocation, but also support the SAR government’s goal of expanding the offshore renminbi liquidity pool and enriching renminbi investment products, he said.

Hui also said Hong Kong handles around 75 percent of offshore renminbi payments, and renminbi deposits in the city stood at 1.3 trillion yuan.

He added that the SAR would continue to enrich renminbi products to further consolidate the city’s position as a global offshore renminbi business hub.

Carlson Tong, chairman of the Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX), also called the listing a milestone for Hong Kong's fixed income and currency (FIC) markets.

“Week by week now, we are seeing the ecosystem in the FIC roadmap created by the [Securities and Futures Commission] and [Hong Kong Monetary Authority] taking shape,” he said.

“Each new listing, each new product, each new tool that gives investors more efficient access to the offshore renminbi bond market is another brick that is added to the structure.”

This was the result of all market stakeholders playing their roles and working together, he added.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hong Kong to help build world-class bay area: CE
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong would actively leverage its advantages of being connected to the mainland and the world under "One Country, Two…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong would actively leverage its advantages of being connected to the mainland and the world under "One Country, Two Systems" to contribute to the national effort to promote bay area economies and build a world-class bay area with other Greater Bay Area cities, Chief Executive John Lee said on Monday.

In a video address to the 16th Hong Kong International Financial Forum and the seventh Pilot "9+2" Navigation GBA Forum, Lee noted that President Xi Jinping proposed establishing a global association for bay areas economic cooperation to deepen exchanges among bay areas around the world and explore new paths for Asia-Pacific cooperation during a keynote speech at the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen last week.

He said this year marks China's year as Apec host, and that the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting and CEO Summit in Shenzhen last week, together with the Apec Finance Ministers' Meeting held in Hong Kong for the first time in October, showed the Greater Bay Area cities' collective role in serving the country's efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community.

Lee said the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, bringing together the two special administrative regions and nine Guangdong cities, had a combined economic output of over US$2.1 trillion, showing strong economic resilience and enormous development potential.

He said the government would deepen coordination with bay area cities on technology and innovation cooperation, "hard connectivity" of infrastructure, "soft connectivity" of rules and mechanisms, and "heart connectivity" among residents, as well as on major cooperation platforms, to promote the efficient flow of people, goods, capital and information.

"Hong Kong will actively leverage its advantages under 'One Country, Two Systems' of connecting the mainland with the world, contribute to our country's development of the bay area economy, and work together with fellow Greater Bay Area cities to build a world-class bay area," he said.

The chief executive said the Northern Metropolis university town would bring together education, technology, industry, talent and urban development, and that the Northern Metropolis would be developed into a "highland" for international talent and an important platform for deeper participation in Greater Bay Area development.

The government, he added, would encourage more top mainland universities and research institutions to set up there.

"We will drive more first-class mainland universities and research institutions to settle in the Northern Metropolis, pool top academic and research capabilities with local colleges and universities to complement each other’s strengths, and serve the country’s high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and self-strengthening," he said.

He also said Hong Kong's common law system, free flow of capital and internationalised business environment allow it to provide bay area enterprises with all-round professional services through a task force on mainland enterprises going global, helping them expand into new markets.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK, region slip even as US stock futures show uptick
articles.excerpt: US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday while Asian markets slid and authorities around the region readied support measures…
articles.fullText:
US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday while Asian markets slid and authorities around the region readied support measures after a withering wipeout last week for tech and chip stocks at the centre of the AI boom.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened down 242 points, or 1.08 percent, at 22,168 and was 395 points lower at one stage in early trading.

The China enterprises index was down 81 points, or 1.08 percent, at 7,472 while the tech index fell 67 points, or 1.9 percent, to 3,443.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 30 points, or 0.86 percent, at 3,503.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 100 points, or 0.98 percent, lower at 10,155 while the ChiNext was down 16 points, or 0.75 percent, at 2,195.

With the Nikkei in Tokyo closed for a public holiday, the Kospi opened 135 points, or 2.77 percent, lower at 4,734 in Seoul before going on a downward spiral to be 207 points down at one stage before noon.

The early losses came as investors still harboured questions over whether the vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI models would generate returns fast enough to repay lenders and big enough to justify some of the high stock prices.

Last week's 10 percent drop in the Nasdaq was its largest weekly drop since pandemic panic gripped markets in March 2020.

Nasdaq 100 futures bounced nearly three percent in early trade on Monday, and S&P 500 futures rose by two percent.

The "AI trade" has for several years lifted a wide range of stocks, from switch and cable makers to electricity generators and the manufacturers of anything in the computing supply chain, but they have been under pressure in recent months from rising interest rates.

AI-related shares took a particularly sharp downturn last week as the exit of Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO nicknamed the "godfather of AI", and the faltering debut of AI company Anthropic, which closed 8.5 percent lower on its first full day of trading, pointed to a souring mood. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Marquez makes history with eighth MotoGP world title
articles.excerpt: Spaniard Marc Marquez was crowned MotoGP world champion for a record-equalling eighth time on Sunday, with an eighth-place finish at…
articles.fullText:
Spaniard Marc Marquez was crowned MotoGP world champion for a record-equalling eighth time on Sunday, with an eighth-place finish at the Portuguese Grand Prix enough to establish an unassailable lead in the standings to cap a remarkable comeback this season.

Italian Marco Bezzecchi rode to victory in southern Portugal but the result was enough to seal a second consecutive world title for the Ducati rider.

On crossing the line, the 33-year-old Marquez leapt from his bike and was hoisted up by his team before he ran towards his fans screaming with his arms aloft.

"Last year was for me, this one is for you," he told his fans through a microphone before again throwing back his head and screaming out his emotions.

His eighth success in the premier class of motorcycling pulled Marquez level with Italian great Giacomo Agostini who won his titles between 1966 and 1975.

The latest triumph is even more remarkable given the Spaniard's injury and crash-blighted campaign where he had to wait until the eighth race in Hungary on June 7 before claiming his first win.

Marquez suffered a flat tyre in the season-opener in Thailand in March, fell at the Spanish GP in Jerez and again at the French GP where he picked up a foot fracture which ruled him out of the following race, the Catalan GP.

Making his comeback at the Italian GP in Mugello he trailed Bezzecchi by a massive 102 points early June just weeks after undergoing foot surgery on top of a previous operation on his injured shoulder.

But the Spaniard managed to bounce back once again, defying those who had already written him off.

Once he got rolling he roared into a regular winning run with seven Grand Prix and ten sprint race victories in all this season.

While not as obviously dominant as having won 11 GP in the 2025 season, where an unexpected return to form since his 2024 switch to Ducati gave him a new lease of life, this latest win is as impressive.

Marquez had been the youngest-ever premier class champion in his debut season in 2013 for Honda and then went on to win the title in five of the next six seasons.

He also overtakes his great rival Valentino Rossi, who won seven MotoGP titles, although the swashbuckling Italian has 89 individual race wins in the top category to Marquez's 80.

Having crashed during Saturday's sprint race Marquez rode out Sunday's GP safely, needing only to finish in the top nine to secure his tenth title across all categories combined.

Aprilia's Bezzecchi won Sunday's race to complete the double in Portugal having also won the sprint, with his stablemate Jorge Martin of Spain crossing in second.

With a total of 439 points and seven victories this year, this was enough for Marquez to keep his rivals at bay.

Martin is second with 396 points but only one win and Bezzecchi, who has 394 points and seven first-place finishes, in third ahead of the season-finale in Valencia, Spain next weekend.

"Thank you for this bike," Marquez told his team Ducati during his victory lap. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Skubal to join Mets in record-breaking deal: reports
articles.excerpt: Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner as Major League Baseball's top pitcher, has agreed to terms on a…
articles.fullText:
Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner as Major League Baseball's top pitcher, has agreed to terms on a record nine-year deal worth US$450 million with the New York Mets, according to multiple reports on Sunday.

The 30-year-old American left-hander spent his first six seasons with the Detroit Tigers before joining the Los Angeles Dodgers in a trade last August, but he was unable to help the club lift a third consecutive World Series trophy.

The US$50 million average annual value would make the deal a record for pitchers, surpassing the US$43.3 million annual value of contracts for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander.

Skubal's deal also would be the richest contract for any pitcher in MLB history, surpassing the mark of US$325 million set when the Dodgers signed Japan's Yoshinobu Yamamoto to a 12-year deal in 2024.

Skubal became only the 12th pitcher in MLB history to win back-to-back Cy Youngs when he captured the award in the American League in 2024 and 2025.

He completed the AL triple crown in 2024, leading the league in wins with 18 and in earned-run average at 2.39 plus topping MLB in strikeouts with 228.

Skubal, a unanimous Cy Young choice in 2024, also had the AL's lowest earned-run average in 2025 at 2.21 and struck out 241 batters over 195 1/3 innings to repeat.

In 2026, he won an arbitration hearing and was awarded US$32 million for the 2026 season, but the campaign was cut short in May when he had to undergo surgery for loose bodies in his elbow.

He returned in July and after joining the Dodgers, Skubal went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 62 innings, then went 1-1 in the playoffs, where the Dodgers were eliminated by eventual champion Milwaukee.

Skubal, considered the top free agent player available, made the agreement as MLB owners and the MLB Players Association stand deadlocked over how to divide profits with the December 1 deadline for a new deal fast approaching.

If the sides cannot agree on terms for a new collective bargaining agreement, a lockout is expected next month.

Owners demand a salary cap system while the union has been against such a format for decades. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday.

After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament.

Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

With his compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998.

"It's been an amazing week. I couldn't finish the week in a better way, so I'm really proud," Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year.

"I've been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I'm playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I've been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me," he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament.

A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles.

But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals.

He lost in the season-ender's final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one.

Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings.

The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three.

The first set of Alcaraz's semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week.

Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold.

Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand.

Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1.

Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native's serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob.

A netted backhand by Zverev – his 19th unforced error of the match – on Alcaraz's first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame.

Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance.

The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points.

But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve.

The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man Utd drubbed 4-0 in nightmare Pochettino debut
articles.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager with a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool that left the Red…
articles.fullText:
Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager with a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool that left the Red Devils still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone.

United never recovered from Leny Yoro's controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool's man advantage count.

Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool's third before Victor Munoz completed the rout.

The defeat leaves United second bottom of the table and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories.

"We feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game," said Pochettino, who was furious at the decision to dismiss Yoro.

"I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card."

Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title.

"We could have scored more," said Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.

"In other games you will remember those chances, but today we've controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box."

Pochettino answered United's call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils' first 10 league games in charge.

The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans.

Pochettino's bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game's decisive moment.

De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal.

The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card.

Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box.

Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar.

Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding.

Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time.

But Bradley Barcola’s blistering speed created Liverpool's third just after the hour mark.

The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home.

Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time.

Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals' pain with chants of "you are going down".

United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football.

The 34 goals they have conceded in all competitions is the worst defensive record of any team in Europe's top five leagues this season. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: FDA clears tiny surgical robot to remove bladder tumors
articles.excerpt: The FDA-authorized Virtuoso Endoscopy System uses needle-sized robotic arms to remove bladder tumors intact, helping pathologists assess detrusor muscle.
articles.fullText:
If a doctor finds a tumor in your bladder, you want to know what you're dealing with. Is it cancer? Has it reached the bladder muscle? The tissue removed during surgery helps answer those questions. Now, a tiny surgical robot could give doctors a clearer view of what's happening inside the bladder.
The FDA has authorized the Virtuoso Endoscopy System, developed by Nashville-based Virtuoso Surgical. It uses two needle-sized robotic arms to remove bladder lesions through the urethra, without cutting through the skin. The technology allows surgeons to remove many tumors in one piece, potentially giving pathologists better tissue samples to examine. This new approach to robotic bladder tumor removal could help doctors make more informed treatment decisions.

WOULD YOU TRUST A TINY DENTAL ROBOT?
The Virtuoso Endoscopy System uses a narrow medical instrument called a rigid endoscope, which enters the bladder through the urethra. At the tip are two miniature robotic arms made from a flexible metal alloy called nitinol. A surgeon controls both arms from a console. One arm lifts and holds the tumor while the other carefully separates it from the tissue underneath. This gives the surgeon two-handed control inside a very small space.
The technique is called en bloc resection, which means removing a tumor in one piece. Surgeons can already perform this procedure using conventional instruments, but it can be technically demanding. Virtuoso designed its system to make that approach easier to perform. The robot also relies entirely on the surgeon's movements. Unlike some autonomous surgical robots being tested in research settings , Virtuoso does not make surgical decisions or operate independently.
Bladder cancer affects thousands of Americans every year. The American Cancer Society estimates that approximately 84,530 people in the United States will receive a bladder cancer diagnosis in 2026. One of the most common procedures for evaluating and removing bladder tumors is called transurethral resection of bladder tumor, or TURBT. During conventional TURBT, surgeons often remove tumors in smaller fragments. While effective for many patients, that approach can disrupt the tissue's original structure. As a result, pathologists may have a harder time determining how deeply cancer has grown. That's particularly important when it comes to the bladder's muscle layer, called the detrusor muscle. Doctors need to know whether cancer has reached this muscle because that can change the recommended treatment.
Removing a lesion intact may preserve more of the information pathologists need. It can also allow them to examine the tissue around the tumor more clearly. Dr. Duke Herrell, a urologic surgeon and CEO of Virtuoso Surgical, explained the potential benefit in the company's FDA announcement. "Removing a tumor intact can provide a better tissue specimen, which supports clearer diagnosis and staging," Herrell said. For patients, a more complete tissue sample could help their medical team determine the next steps with greater confidence.
Virtuoso has already tested the system in human patients, and the early clinical findings are encouraging. In the first 20 patients enrolled in the company-sponsored VIABLE study at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, 94% of removed lesions contained detrusor muscle. That exceeded the study's predefined performance goal of 60%. Researchers also reported that surgical margins could be evaluated in 93% of malignant lesions. Surgical margins are the edges of the removed tissue. Examining them can help doctors assess whether cancer cells extend to the edge of the sample. However, being able to evaluate a margin does not necessarily mean it is free of cancer. The company reported no adverse events during the operations.
There are important limitations to these findings. The study involved a small number of patients at one medical center. The previously published first phase of the same VIABLE study involved six patients and recorded two postoperative adverse events. One patient experienced temporary urinary retention, while another developed a chest infection later linked to a separate esophageal tumor. The company also compared its results with previously published research on conventional bladder tumor removal.
However, the Virtuoso study did not directly compare the robot against traditional instruments in a randomized trial. Researchers still need larger studies to determine whether the system improves long-term outcomes or reduces the need for additional procedures.
BRAIN TUMOR FOUND DURING PREVENTIVE SCAN PUTS FULL-BODY MRIS BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT
The FDA granted De Novo authorization for the Virtuoso Endoscopy System on Oct. 30, 2026. The company publicly announced the decision on Nov. 10. The authorization establishes a new FDA classification for robotic surgical instruments that operate through an endoscope inside the body. Specifically, the system is authorized to remove bladder lesions in adult patients and obtain tissue samples, including bladder muscle, to assist in diagnosing bladder cancer .
The decision follows the FDA's September 2025 Breakthrough Device Designation for the system. That earlier designation recognized the technology's potential and allowed the company to receive additional regulatory guidance during development. However, the new authorization does not establish that the robot improves survival rates or prevents cancer from returning. The system must also be operated by trained surgeons in an operating room.
Virtuoso Surgical plans a limited U.S. launch in 2027, starting with leading urology centers. The company has not announced which hospitals will receive the system first. That means patients may have to wait before the technology becomes available at their local hospital. Questions also remain about pricing and insurance coverage.
Virtuoso is exploring other potential applications for its miniature robotic instruments, including procedures involving the lungs. However, those uses remain experimental and have not received FDA authorization. For now, the company's focus is bladder surgery, where better tissue samples could help doctors evaluate cancer more accurately.
If you or someone you love is facing bladder cancer, this technology could eventually provide another surgical option. Its miniature robotic arms may help doctors obtain more complete tissue samples during the initial procedure. However, availability will be limited at first, and the early results still need confirmation in larger studies. The robot's FDA authorization also does not guarantee better results for every patient.
If you're discussing bladder tumor surgery with a urologist, ask whether en bloc resection might be appropriate for your situation. You should also ask how the surgeon plans to obtain enough tissue to determine whether cancer has reached the bladder muscle. Those answers can help you understand your options before surgery.
When you're facing a possible cancer diagnosis, getting accurate answers as early as possible can make a real difference. That's what I like about this technology. Virtuoso's tiny robotic arms could help surgeons collect better tissue samples without taking control away from the medical professional performing the operation. It's also encouraging to see the FDA authorize a system designed for such a specific surgical challenge. Still, 20 patients represent a very small study, and I want to see how this robot performs in larger trials before getting too excited about its potential. If the results hold up, this could become a valuable addition to the tools doctors use to diagnose bladder cancer.
