articles.title: Tech stocks slump, leaving Nasdaq in red for the year
articles.excerpt: A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7 percent, dragging the index to…
articles.fullText:
A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7 percent, dragging the index to its worst weekly loss in more than 18 months, and knocking the Nasdaq composite into the red for the year.

The S&P 500 fell 265.44 points to 6,910.39. The Dow dropped 949.73 points to 48,147.33, and the Nasdaq lost 1,261.47 points to close at 22,617.73.

The benchmark index is now in what professional investors call a “correction,” having fallen more than 10 percent from its October 6 all-time high.

The last time the S&P 500 had a correction was March 2025, as the Trump administration’s trade war rattled the market. Its weekly loss, marking its worst such decline since April 2025, as the trade war escalated, capped a seven-day losing streak, the longest such string of losses since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020.

The Nasdaq composite slumped 5.3 percent, pulling it into negative territory for the year. Its weekly loss was also just shy of its worst week since March 2020.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, with less exposure to technology stocks, fell 1.9 percent.

Chip stocks like Nvidia, Micron Technology, Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices bore the brunt of the selling, but other companies connected to the AI buildout tanked as well, including the optical products company Corning and the energy provider Bloom Energy. The AI lab Anthropic, coming off a successful IPO Thursday, tumbled 9.1 percent.

The AI trade has been losing steam partly over worries that AI stocks’ big market values and heavy spending are unjustified. Fears of a bubble within the sector have also been exacerbated by the results of the recent midterm elections, with candidates advocating for a slowdown in data centre construction winning at both the federal and state level.

“The whole notion that AI can continue to spend unlimited amounts of money and support the stock market, I think the notion of that is ending as we speak, that’s what’s being priced right now,” said Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird. “But I don’t think that means that the overall bull market that started in October 2022 is over.”

Much of the AI rout was centred among chip stocks, which have been big beneficiaries of the build out of AI data centres. Advanced Micro Devices sank 13.3 percent, Micron Technology slid 13.9 percent and Broadcom fell 12.1 percent.

Nvidia, considered by many to be the poster child for the AI boom, fell for the ninth day in the last 10, closing 13.8 percent lower. The chip company’s stock was caught up in the market’s anxiety about the strength of the AI build out, and more recently has been pressured by worries about its future following the sudden downfall of Jensen Huang, its former CEO and co-founder. Since the Huang scandal erupted earlier this month, the stock has dropped more than 25 percent.

The big market debut for Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI tool, fizzled on Friday with the rest of the tech sector. The stock fell 9.1 percent to US$88.30, but remains above its IPO price of US$83 per share. It was the biggest public stock offering ever, at one point surpassing US$2 trillion in value. (AP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Uber Parking could save you from circling the block
articles.excerpt: Uber Parking launches in 15 U.S. cities after the SpotHero deal, offering upfront prices, Uber One credits, and a future…
articles.fullText:
You finally make it downtown for dinner, but now comes the real challenge. Finding somewhere to park. You circle the block once, then again. Before you know it, you're late and getting frustrated. Sound familiar? Well, Uber thinks it has a solution. The company just launched Uber Parking, a new feature that lets you reserve a parking spot directly through the Uber app before you even leave home. Yes, the same company that built its business around getting you into someone else's car now wants to help when you drive your own. And there's another interesting twist. Uber has plans for those parking garages that involve robotaxis.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
UBER LETS PARENTS WATCH TEEN RIDES LIVE
On Nov. 9, Uber announced the launch of Uber Parking, bringing parking reservations directly into its app. The feature follows Uber's acquisition of SpotHero, a popular parking reservation service. Through that deal, Uber gained access to a network of more than 13,000 parking garages, lots and valet locations across more than 400 cities in the United States and Canada.
So, instead of driving around looking for parking, you can search for an available spot near your destination. You can also see the price upfront, making it easier to decide whether driving makes financial sense. For someone heading into the city for dinner or trying to get to an important appointment, that could save some aggravation. And if you've ever paid a small fortune to park somewhere, you'll probably appreciate being able to compare prices before arriving.
Uber has made the process pretty simple. You can book parking using the same app you already use to request a ride.
Here's how it works:
Once you've booked, your digital parking pass appears inside the Uber app. Depending on the location, you'll either scan a QR code or enter through a system that recognizes your license plate. Uber also says you can extend reservations through the app if you need more time. Cancellation policies vary by parking facility. Some reservations qualify for a full refund if canceled before the scheduled start time. Always check the booking terms before paying.
One thing worth mentioning: Uber generally won't physically park your car for you. Unless you choose a valet location, you'll still be the one behind the wheel.
FAKE E-ZPASS EMAIL THREATENS $100 FINE OVER UNPAID TOLL
Uber Parking launched in 15 U.S. cities on Nov. 9.
Those cities are:
Uber plans to expand the service into additional markets. However, there's an important detail here. Although SpotHero operates across more than 400 cities, Uber Parking has not yet expanded throughout that entire network. Also, the new feature is still rolling out. So, even if you're in one of the launch cities, you may not see the Parking icon immediately. First, make sure you're using the latest version of the Uber app. You can also visit SpotHero's website to search for parking in areas where the Uber feature is unavailable.
Here's a little bonus if you already pay for Uber One. Uber says eligible members can earn 10% back in Uber One credits on qualifying parking reservations once their parking session is complete. You can use those credits toward future eligible Uber rides or Uber Eats orders. For example, if you spend $30 on a qualifying parking reservation, you could earn $3 in Uber One credits.
That may not sound like a fortune. However, if you're regularly parking downtown, those credits could add up. Just keep in mind that the 10% reward only applies to eligible reservations. You also need an active Uber One membership to qualify and redeem the credits. And remember, these are Uber credits rather than cash back to your bank account. Before booking, compare the total parking price with other nearby options. A cheaper garage could still save you more money than the rewards you'd earn.
Uber also sees parking garages as part of its future robotaxi business . Think about it. When a driverless taxi drops someone off, what happens next? If another passenger needs a ride nearby, that's easy enough. But what happens when nobody needs the car? Does it keep driving around until another request comes in? That could mean more empty vehicles on already crowded streets. Uber is reportedly exploring ways to use parking facilities as waiting areas for autonomous vehicles. Instead of driving around without passengers, robotaxis could pull into nearby garages and wait for their next assignment.
Then, when someone requests a ride, the vehicle could head out to pick them up. Uber believes that approach could reduce unnecessary driving and help lower operating costs. There's another potential benefit. Keeping autonomous vehicles in nearby facilities could make it easier to have them ready when demand increases. However, this remains a developing plan. Uber has not announced that every SpotHero garage will accommodate robotaxis, and the company has not provided a timeline for a broad rollout of these facilities. For now, the immediate focus remains helping people find parking for their own cars.
There's something else worth paying attention to here. For years, Uber built its business around giving people an alternative to driving. Now, the company wants you opening its app even when you plan to take your own car. Let's say you're going downtown for dinner. You could check the price of an Uber ride. Then, you could compare that with the cost of driving and parking.
If driving looks cheaper, you can reserve a space through Uber. If taking a ride makes more sense, you can book that instead. Either way, Uber stays part of your plans. And as autonomous vehicles become more common, the company could eventually use that same parking network to support its robotaxi partners. It's an interesting strategy, especially as Uber looks for more ways to keep people using its app.
The biggest benefit is pretty straightforward. You may be able to reserve parking before leaving home and spend less time driving around looking for an available spot. That could be especially useful when you're heading somewhere unfamiliar or trying to make a flight. However, there are a few things I'd recommend checking before you book.
Don't assume Uber offers the lowest rate. Check the final price against other parking options before paying. Also, make sure your reservation covers the time you'll actually need.
Some parking garages have height limits. If you drive a larger SUV or truck, check those restrictions before booking. Also, confirm the exact entrance address, which may differ from the garage's street address.
Some parking reservations can be canceled for free before they begin, but the rules vary by location. Review the specific garage's cancellation terms before booking. Once your reservation starts, Uber says it can no longer be canceled or refunded.
Some garages use QR codes for entry. That's convenient, but criminals have also placed fake QR codes on parking meters to trick drivers into visiting fraudulent payment websites. Use the parking pass provided directly through your Uber app rather than scanning an unfamiliar sticker. We've previously reported on how criminals use fake parking QR codes to steal money.
Even with a reservation, finding your car afterward can still be a headache. Fortunately, Google Maps and Apple Maps have tools that can help you remember where you parked. Our guide to finding your parked car with Maps explains how to set them up.
I think Uber is onto something here. Who hasn't wasted time driving around looking for parking, especially when you're already running late? Being able to reserve a spot before leaving home sounds pretty convenient. Of course, I'd want to make sure I'm getting a good price. But what really caught my attention is Uber's plan to use parking garages for robotaxis. Having driverless cars park between rides makes sense, especially if it means fewer empty vehicles clogging up our streets. Still, I wonder what happens when those garages start filling up with robotaxis. Will there be enough room for the rest of us? That's something I'll be watching as this technology takes off.
Would you trust Uber to handle your parking reservations, or do you worry that parking garages could eventually become crowded with robotaxis, leaving fewer spaces for the rest of us? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: Spain, France to clash in Nations League quarter-final
articles.excerpt: World champions Spain will face France, while England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the Uefa Nations League, after…
articles.fullText:
World champions Spain will face France, while England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the Uefa Nations League, after the draw took place on Friday.

Spain beat France 2-0 in the semi-finals of the World Cup in the United States in July, on the way to winning the trophy. They also defeated Les Bleus 5-4 in the semi-finals of the last edition of the Nations League, last year.

"This will not be about getting revenge for the World Cup semi-final," Zinedine Zidane, who was appointed France coach following that tournament, told L'Equipe.

"We knew we were going to get a strong opponent and we have got the reigning world champions."

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs in late March, with Spain at home first after coming second in Group A3, while France topped Group A1.

Spain won the Nations League in 2023, while France beat them to win the 2021 final.

England topped Group A3 on goal difference after beating Spain away in their last outing, and their reward is a two-legged last-eight tie against Norway with the first leg on Norwegian soil.

England edged Norway in the World Cup quarter-finals this year before losing to Argentina in the semi-finals.

The other quarter-final ties pitched reigning Nations League champions Portugal against the Netherlands, and Belgium against Germany.

"So much can happen in the time between now and then," Germany coach Jurgen Klopp told the German team's in-house broadcaster, DFB TV.

"We're very happy with the last impression we left, but we're also fully aware that we are right at the beginning of a development process," added Klopp, whose team topped Group A2 after thrashing the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin on Monday.

"We want to carry this positive momentum forward. There's still a great deal of work to be done."

The winners of the quarter-finals will advance to the final stages, which will be held in June in a venue yet to be decided.

Spain or France will play the Netherlands or Portugal in the semis, with England facing Belgium or Germany should they get past Norway.

The Nations League quarter-finals and play-offs in March will all take place at the same time as qualifying begins for Euro 2028. (AFP)

articles.title: Hackers use Microsoft Outlook security flaw to steal your login data
articles.excerpt: Microsoft Outlook flaw CVE-2026-124194 lets a malicious .msg file expose NTLMv2 authentication data, and Microsoft confirms hackers already exploited it.
articles.fullText:
You probably know better than to enter your password on a suspicious website. But what if hackers could steal information tied to your Windows login without ever asking for your password? That's the concern behind a Microsoft Outlook security flaw that hackers are already exploiting. Attackers can trick someone into opening a malicious Outlook file that quietly exposes Windows authentication information. That information could help a criminal impersonate you and potentially gain access to systems you use.
Microsoft released a fix on Nov. 10. However, the company confirms hackers were exploiting the vulnerability before the update became available. If you use Outlook for work, this is one security update you should check right away.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
FAKE AI EVENT INVITES TARGET MICROSOFT AND GOOGLE LOGINS
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194, involves how Outlook handles specially crafted message files. An attacker can create a malicious Outlook message file, such as one using the .msg format. The hacker then needs to convince someone to open that file in an affected version of Outlook. Once opened, the malicious file can cause Outlook to connect to a server controlled by the attacker. That connection happens without the usual warning about accessing external content. During the connection, Windows can reveal NTLMv2 authentication information . This data helps Windows verify your identity when connecting to certain network services.
The information differs from your actual password. However, hackers may be able to use it in a follow-up attack to impersonate you. For someone using Outlook at work, that could potentially expose company resources their account can access. The outcome depends on the network's security protections and whether the attacker can successfully misuse the authentication information. Here's what makes this especially concerning. The attack doesn't require you to type your password into a fake login page. Opening the malicious file can be enough if your computer can connect to the attacker's network location. Microsoft says simply viewing the message through Outlook's Preview Pane does not trigger this particular vulnerability. Someone must open the malicious file for the attack to work.
Microsoft included the Outlook fix in its November Patch Tuesday security updates. The company's core release addressed 1,093 vulnerabilities, including 63 rated critical. Interestingly, Microsoft classified this particular Outlook vulnerability as moderate, giving it a CVSS severity score of 6.5 out of 10. However, that rating tells only part of the story. Microsoft confirms attackers have already exploited the flaw. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) also added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov. 10. In other words, hackers are already taking advantage of this security weakness. Microsoft has not publicly identified who carried out the attacks or disclosed how many people were affected. The company also hasn't provided detailed information about the incidents. With hackers already exploiting the flaw, it's important to install the security update as soon as possible.
FAKE CHATGPT BILLING EMAILS CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN
According to Microsoft's security advisory, the affected products include:
The vulnerability concerns affected desktop Office installations on Windows computers. Microsoft's advisory does not list Outlook.com in a web browser or the Outlook mobile apps as affected products. If your employer manages your Microsoft 365 software, your IT department may handle these updates. However, it's worth confirming that the security fix has been installed. For people who manage their own computers, here's how to check.
The most important thing you can do is update Microsoft Office. However, a few additional precautions can help reduce your exposure to suspicious files and account attacks.
Microsoft has released security updates addressing the vulnerability. You can manually check for updates in supported Windows versions of Office.
If you don't see Update Now, you may need to select Enable Updates first. If the entire Update Options menu is missing, your employer may manage updates centrally. Contact your IT department rather than assuming the software has already been patched. You can also review Microsoft's official Office update instructions.
After installing the update, you can check which version of Office is running on your computer.
For affected volume-licensed installations, Microsoft's November 10 security release includes these updated builds:
These build numbers apply to the specified LTSC editions. They shouldn't be used to check other Office versions. If you're using Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, the correct build depends on your organization's update channel. You can check Microsoft's Office security release notes or contact your IT department to confirm the fix.
Although this vulnerability requires an Office fix, keeping Windows updated remains important.
On Windows 11:
Next, check whether Windows can receive updates for other Microsoft products.
This can help Windows deliver updates for supported Microsoft products. However, some Office installations receive updates through separate services or employer-managed systems. Remember that checking Windows Update alone may not confirm you've installed the specific Outlook fix. Check Office separately. It's also smart to back up important files before installing major operating system updates.
A message file from an unfamiliar sender deserves extra caution, especially if you weren't expecting it. Watch for attachments ending in .msg, a common file format for saved Outlook messages. The format itself is legitimate. However, attackers can abuse it to deliver this exploit. If an email claims you need to open an attached message to review an invoice or urgent workplace request, verify it through another trusted channel. Even attachments appearing to come from coworkers deserve a second look when the request seems unusual.
If something looks suspicious, avoid opening the attachment. Instead, report the message using Outlook's built-in reporting tools when available.
In supported versions of Outlook:
The exact menu location depends on your Outlook version and your employer's settings. If you're using a work account and don't see a reporting option, contact your IT department. Avoid forwarding the suspicious attachment to other coworkers.
Strong antivirus software can help identify suspicious attachments and malicious activity before they cause further damage. Look for protection that includes real-time scanning and behavior-based detection. These features may help catch threats that traditional virus signatures miss. However, antivirus software cannot replace Microsoft's security patch. Installing the Outlook update remains essential for closing this particular vulnerability. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
Multifactor authentication (MFA) adds another layer of account protection by requiring additional verification when you sign in. Enable it on your Microsoft account and other important services whenever available. Keep in mind that MFA may not stop attacks involving stolen Windows authentication information. That's another reason updating Outlook takes priority.
If you recently opened an unexpected Outlook message attachment, don't assume everything is fine because nothing unusual appeared on your screen. Here's what to do next.
One important reminder: Changing your password alone may not address every potential exposure from this vulnerability. If you opened the attachment on a work computer, let your IT team determine whether additional security measures are necessary.
Microsoft's November security release covers far more than Outlook. It also fixes weaknesses that could allow attackers to gain additional privileges or remotely execute malicious code. For those of you using a Windows PC every day, the sheer number of vulnerabilities may sound overwhelming. However, not every flaw carries the same immediate risk. In this case, the Outlook weakness deserves your attention because Microsoft has confirmed active exploitation.
The larger concern is how easily a malicious file can take advantage of trusted software. Outlook is part of everyday communication for countless businesses, and opening saved email messages may seem harmless. This vulnerability shows why keeping Office updated deserves the same attention as updating Windows.
What concerns me about this Outlook flaw is how little someone has to do to put their information at risk. You could receive what looks like a routine work attachment, open it and unknowingly expose information that helps a hacker impersonate you. There's no obvious warning telling you something went wrong. And by the time you realize it, the damage may already be done. I also find it troubling that Microsoft rated this vulnerability moderate even though attackers were already exploiting it. Most people aren't going to spend their day reviewing security ratings, and they shouldn't have to. They need software that protects them and updates that are easy to install. My advice is simple. If you use Outlook on a Windows computer, check for Office updates today. Don't assume your computer has already taken care of it.
Should Microsoft be doing more to prevent a single malicious Outlook file from exposing your login information, or do you think keeping your software updated is enough protection? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: Hong Kong inflation remains moderate at 2.2pc
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong's consumer inflation remained moderate in October, with overall prices rising by 2.2 percent year on year. The figure…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong's consumer inflation remained moderate in October, with overall prices rising by 2.2 percent year on year.

The figure, published by the Census and Statistics Department on Friday, compared with the 1.9 percent expansion in September, although the government attributed the larger increase last month to the end of the rates concession.

For the first 10 months of 2026, the composite consumer price index (CPI) rose by 1.8 percent over the same period a year ago.

Netting out the effects of the government's one-off relief measures, the underlying inflation in October stood at two percent, compared to 2.1 percent in September.

Breaking down the various components of the composite CPI, prices jumped by 12.7 percent for electricity, gas and water and 11.4 percent for health services.

Transport costs, which are sensitive to rising fuel prices, increased by 4.5 percent.

There were milder increases for necessities such as food, which edged up by 0.3 percent, while housing rents ticked up 1.4 percent.

A government spokesman noted that the prices of fuel-related items continued to rise noticeably.

"But spillover effects remained limited, with prices of most other items increasing modestly or declining," he said.

Looking ahead, the spokesman said price pressures on other fronts should remain broadly in check, although geopolitical tensions remain a key source of near-term uncertainty for international fuel prices.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK, mainland slip as tech stocks take brunt of fears
articles.excerpt: Mainland and Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Friday, with tech shares leading losses after a steep Wall Street…
articles.fullText:
Mainland and Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Friday, with tech shares leading losses after a steep Wall Street selloff weighed on investor sentiment, while Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO did little to revive waning optimism surrounding the artificial intelligence sector.

The benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 430 points, or 1.9 percent, lower at 22,410 on turnover of HK$270.3 billion.

The tech index dived 138 points, or 3.8 percent, to 3,511 while the China enterprises index was 135 points, or 1.8 percent, down at 7,554.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index closed down 43 points, or 1.22 percent, at 3,533 on turnover of 702.57 billion yuan while the blue-chip CSI300 index lost 0.8 percent.

Both indexes recorded their lowest closing levels since July 2025.

For the week, the Shanghai Composite fell 2.8 percent to notch the biggest weekly drop since July, and the CSI300 lost 1.5 percent.

Investor sentiment was also weighed down by signs that Washington is tightening tech curbs on China, despite meetings between the leaders of the world's two largest economies this week.

The Shenzhen Component Index closed down 326 points, or 3.09 percent, at 10,256 on turnover of 719.62 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index closed down 81 points, or 3.54 percent, at 2,212 on turnover of 334.97 billion yuan.

The decline came after US stocks slumped on Thursday, as AI-related shares came under pressure following Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO's failure to sustain an early rally.

"The optimism failed to lift the broader AI sector, as concerns over stretched valuations and elevated capex spending continued to weigh on sentiment," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

In China, tech sectors that require huge computing power, such as big data, AI and cloud computing all fell sharply.

Hong Kong-listed shares of Chinese AI model developers, which rely heavily on advanced computing power, also tumbled.

Minimax slumped 10.8 percent to record lows, bringing this week's loss to more than 30 percent.

Z.AI shares declined 7.2 percent, bringing the weekly loss to 18.2 percent.

Semiconductor shares were among the biggest drags, with a subindex tracking the sector plunging 3.9 percent.

Sentiment towards chipmakers was also hurt by TSMC tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers, suspending some previously permitted advanced manufacturing orders and generally limiting affected customers to older chipmaking technology, sources said.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended 3,007 points, or 5.06 percent, at 56,436 amid chip and tech related plunges of 10.32 percent for Advantest, 7.06 percent for Tokyo Electron, 14.48 percent for technology investor SoftBank Group and 11.66 percent for memory chip maker Kioxia.

For the week, the index lost 7.7 percent.

The broader Topix fell 148 points, or 3.88 percent, to 3,674 for the day.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 267 points, or 5.21 percent, at 4,869 as chipmaker losses of 7.01 percent piled up for Samsung Electronics and 5.92 percent for SK Hynix. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Beijing warns of 'judicial overreach' in ICJ ruling
articles.excerpt: China raised concerns of judicial overreach after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its…
articles.fullText:
China raised concerns of judicial overreach after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, saying on Friday "such practices are not conducive" to a resolution.

"China is concerned about issues such as jurisdiction overreach and expanded interpretation, and believes that such practices are not conducive to the settlement of disputes," Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said when asked about the ICJ ruling.

"The international community should make joint efforts in this direction to avoid complicating this issue," he added.

Guo was speaking as Malaysia said it would resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Türkiye through a structured skills training programme, in what would be one of the biggest resettlement initiatives involving the Rohingya.

The proposal is part of the government's efforts to address the Rohingya refugee situation in Malaysia in a more "coordinated, effective and humane manner", Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said in a statement.

"I welcome the government of Türkiye's agreement to receive 10,000 Rohingya refugees. This marks an important step in Malaysia's efforts to find a long-term solution to an issue that has long posed challenges for migration management and national security," he said.

Ahmad Zahid said the initiative with Türkiye could serve as a model for how countries can work together to manage refugee resettlement. (AFP/Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Former Secret Service investigator sounds alarm over AI scams as Americans grow increasingly anxious
articles.excerpt: Former Secret Service cyberfraud investigator Jason Brown warns AI voice cloning scams could trick families into losing thousands of dollars…
articles.fullText:
A former Secret Service cyberfraud investigator warned that Americans are increasingly on edge following a wave of major technology disruptions , while artificial intelligence is making scams targeting families and consumers more sophisticated.
Jason Brown, a former U.S. Secret Service cyberfraud investigator and iCounter's director of customer advisory and counter fraud lead, told Fox News Digital on Thursday that Americans have reason to be increasingly cautious about technology.
"Everybody's on edge," Brown said.
"There's been a lot of stuff that has happened in the past week in particular that people are concerned about," he continued, citing recent technology outages involving Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and several financial institutions.
TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS
Brown acknowledged that some incidents involved infrastructure problems while others remained under investigation.
With the holiday season approaching, Brown warned that AI has made it easier for criminals to create convincing fraudulent messages , eliminating many of the warning signs consumers previously relied on.
"AI has just made the criminal a lot more efficient and a little bit more effective," Brown said.
Spelling mistakes, poor grammar and awkward phrasing — once common indicators of fraudulent messages — are becoming less reliable as criminals use AI to generate more convincing communications, he explained.
AI VOICE SCAM TRAPS MOM IN 5-HOUR KIDNAPPING NIGHTMARE
AI also allows criminals to impersonate familiar voices , potentially tricking victims into believing they are speaking with a family member in distress.
Brown described a scenario in which a scammer uses a short voice recording to impersonate someone's relative and demand thousands of dollars in gift cards.
"AI just makes them a lot more efficient and a lot less prone to errors," he said, warning that Americans must become more skeptical of suspicious messages.
"Unfortunately, we're at a point where everybody needs to have that level of distrust," he said.
As holiday shopping ramps up, Brown said scammers are likely to impersonate major delivery companies, including UPS, FedEx and the U.S. Postal Service.
FAKE E-ZPASS EMAIL THREATENS $100 FINE OVER UNPAID TOLL
He warned that fraudulent messages may claim packages cannot be delivered until additional postage is paid, with scammers demanding payment through cryptocurrency or gift cards.
"If it comes from crypto, especially if it comes from gift cards, that's a red flag for sure," Brown said.
Beyond the emotional toll, Brown warned that increasingly sophisticated scams can result in significant financial losses. He cited FBI reporting that he said identified more than 22,000 AI-related fraud cases in 2025, with losses exceeding $890 million.
Brown noted that businesses are also vulnerable to schemes in which criminals impersonate trusted vendors and redirect legitimate payments into fraudulent accounts.
AGING MEANS LEARNING HOW TO PREVENT COSTLY SCAMS TARGETING OLDER AMERICANS
The holiday season can create additional vulnerabilities as executives travel, employees take time off and temporary workers join company operations, he said.
Brown urged Americans to independently verify suspicious messages and take additional precautions when communicating with family members, including establishing a "safe word" to help confirm someone's identity during an unexpected call.
"Another thing that we always talk about with family members, set up a safe word ahead of time. Have that conversation now," he said, adding that even if a caller provides the correct word, people should still end the call and contact the person independently using a trusted number.
"The biggest safety valve for anybody in a scam when it comes over the internet via your cell phone, over the computer is stop, think and then independently verify," he added.

articles.title: HK 'can blossom amid growth in regionalism'
articles.excerpt: China experts on Friday urged Hong Kong to carve out a new economic strategy and lean into regional growth while…
articles.fullText:
China experts on Friday urged Hong Kong to carve out a new economic strategy and lean into regional growth while warning that global energy policies remained at odds with climate goals.

Their comments came a day after the Apec summit wrapped up in Shenzhen, where talks and discussions centred on Asia-Pacific trade and economic cooperation, technology and innovation, and major-power diplomacy.

Speaking on RTHK's Backchat programme on Friday, Einar Tangen, a senior fellow at the Centre for International Governance Innovation, said global trade was shifting towards regional blocs and that Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area had a strategic role to play within Asia.

“The world is dividing, and you can quite clearly see the growth of regionalism and this is what Apec was about, and then you have entities within that sphere like Hong Kong and Greater Bay Area, which are there to serve it,” he said.

“It doesn't mean that they will not have robust interactions with Europe and America and etc, but they form a vital function in an emerging economy where China and Asean are now beyond one trillion dollars.”

Tangen also noted that it’s time to start re-evaluating and seeing the Global South more as a primary focus for development opportunities, where Hong Kong and Shenzhen are going to blossom and serve the region.

For his part, Victor Gao, vice president of the Centre for China and Globalisation, suggested the city come up with a new strategy for ways to deal with upcoming challenges and opportunities.

The relative advantages that Hong Kong has enjoyed for many years ago now is fast dwindling, he said, and it should learn from the great example of places such as Shenzhen and always be committed to pushing forward to scale real heights.

Gao emphasised that complacency, inefficiency or a failure to reach new heights will likely hinder Hong Kong’s prospects for major economic and financial achievements in the coming years.

Josef Gregory Mahoney, professor of politics and international relations at East China Normal University, gave his take on the outcome of the trilateral summit involving China, the United States and Russia at the Apec summit.

He noted that while China was working to accelerate green transformation and reduce global carbon emissions, both the US and Russia remained heavily reliant on fossil fuels.

“The thing that concerns me most about the declaration is that you have two fossil fuel-dependent economies, Russia and the United States, and you have China, which is trying to accelerate green transformations and make the world less dependent on climate change-causing energy carbon emissions,” Mahoney said.

He also pointed out that the ongoing global energy shock stemmed from the conflict with Ukraine as well as US actions involving Venezuela and Iran, saying a resolution to increase oil production runs counter to broader climate goals.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: PNG has the legal right to close down Taiwan’s office, but at what cost?
articles.excerpt: After Taiwan pulls out of Port Moresby, analysts weigh the pros and cons of closer ties with China.
articles.fullText:
PORT MORESBY, Papua New Guinea – The decision by Papua New Guinea to order Taiwan’s representative office in Port Moresby to close is well within the country’s legal rights, but the legal and geopolitical considerations for such a decision are distinct, a commercial lawyer based in the South Pacific country told Radio Free Asia.
In July , PNG’s Foreign Affairs Minister Justin Tkatchenko announced in an official statement the immediate cessation of operations and the formal closure of the physical presence of the Chinese Taipei Economic Office, citing Port Moresby’s recognition of Beijing.
The office served as Taiwan’s de facto diplomatic mission in PNG, facilitating trade and other exchanges despite the absence of formal diplomatic relations between the two sides.
Taiwan on Nov. 6 confirmed the office would shut down, its personnel would withdraw, and all technical missions, scholarship and training programs would cease. Taipei also announced that it would stop spot purchases of PNG’s liquefied natural gas, or LNG, Port Moresby’s largest export commodity. Prior to the closure, Taiwan had purchased about a third of PNG’s LNG exports.
The decision to force Taiwan to close its representative office is less a legal matter than a policy decision, Margareth Parua, a Port Moresby-based commercial lawyer, told RFA.
“On the information presently available, there is no clearly identified international legal obligation requiring PNG to close an unofficial Taiwanese trade office merely because it recognises the People’s Republic of China,” she said. “Given the longstanding economic and commercial relationship between PNG and Taiwan, it would be regrettable if the decision resulted in the unnecessary loss of trade, investment and other opportunities for our people.”
Weighing options
One year after PNG gained its independence from Australia in 1975, it recognized Beijing diplomatically, adopting its own version of a “One-China Policy” which closely aligns with Beijing’s “One-China Principle” that there is only one China, Taiwan is a part of China, and that the government in Beijing is the sole legal government of China. This differs from the One China Policy of the United States in that Washington’s policy merely acknowledges Beijing’s stance on Taiwan without agreeing or disagreeing with it.
Neither Port Moresby’s One-China Policy precluded unofficial relations with Taiwan, but Beijing has recently leveraged its economic might to pressure Pacific island countries in an effort to further isolate Taiwan, Jonah Bock, assistant director for research at the Alliance Futures Initiative, a Washington-based think tank, told RFA shortly after Tkatchenko’s announcement in July.
“China will continue to aggressively pursue any action that reduces Taiwan’s international space – its ethos of national rejuvenation relies on unification. It is not an option for China to stop the contest,” said Bock in July. “The move is to curry favor with the PRC and the goal is vast sums of Chinese money.”
China's President Xi Jinping (R) shakes hands with Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape before leaders take a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on Nov. 19, 2026.
(Greg Baker/Pool via Reuters) Parua said that PNG should carefully consider whether forcing Taipei to close its representative office was necessary to maintain its One-China Policy, and whether the benefits of doing so outweigh the costs to national interest.
The biggest risk might have been the loss of LNG sales to Taiwan, but closer ties with China can make up for that, Joseph Ealedona, a Papua New Guinean senior journalist and former media executive, told RFA.
“While we lost the gas sales, discussions are taking place for China to purchase more gas to cover for this,” he said. “It’s a positive decision given our deep relations with China and the many benefits we can take from China. China is a massive economy and we must maintain our relations with them.”
Meanwhile, PNG’s former Prime Minister Peter O’Neill commented in Port Moresby-based weekly English daily The National that the country had lost a major buyer in Taiwan, and criticized current Prime Minister James Marape saying he traded Taiwan for China and 191 million kina (US$42.2 million).
Taipei disappointed, Washington concerned, but Beijing jubilant
Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed regret in its official statement on Nov. 6 announcing the closure of the representative office. The statement detailed how Taiwan had given Papua New Guinea economic, agricultural, developmental and medical support over the years.
“Regrettably, the foundation of mutual trust, established through long-term bilateral collaboration, has been seriously undermined by the recent actions of the government of Papua New Guinea,” the statement said. “The situation also reflects China’s continued use of political pressure and economic influence to interfere in the diplomatic decisions of other nations and suppress Taiwan’s international participation.”
The statement also said that the change would have a “substantial impact” on PNG’s natural gas exports.
A man walks in front of flags of Honduras, Taiwan, and other countries, displayed at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs building, in Taipei, Taiwan on March 23, 2023.
(Annabelle Chih/Reuters) A U.S. State Department spokesperson told RFA on Nov. 9 that Washington was “deeply concerned” that PNG had ordered Taipei’s office in Port Moresby closed.
“Taiwan is a reliable, likeminded, and democratic partner, and its relationships around the world provide significant benefits to the citizens of those countries, including Papua New Guinea,” the spokesperson said. “This is yet another example of Beijing’s intimidation campaign against Taiwan and its supporters around the world, which undermines the sovereign decisions of countries choosing to partner with Taiwan and threatens international peace and prosperity.”
The Chinese Embassy in Port Moresby on Nov. 10 said in a statement that the PNG government made the right decision, and criticized Taiwan’s statement as being full of “lies and empty threats.”
“We highly appreciate and applaud the PNG Government’s firm adherence to one-China principle and the concrete measures to implement this principle, which will further consolidate the political foundation for China-PNG bilateral relations and cooperation in various fields,” the statement said. “If the Taiwan side reduces its LNG imports from PNG, the loss will on its side instead of PNG side.”
Beijing also said spot purchases of PNG’s LNG would find new buyers, including China.
“As to Taiwan’s ‘assistance’ to PNG, it is almost nothing compared to the aid and assistance from China’s mainland.”
Additional reporting by Eugene Whong in Washington. Edited by Taejun Kang and Eugene Whong.

articles.title: 'China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners'
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or fundamental conflicts of interests.

China-Australia relations are stable at present, he said when meeting Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen.

Xi said that in a volatile and turbulent world, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the right direction of friendship and cooperation.

China and Australia have brought about a comprehensive turnaround in bilateral relations, he said.

Xi called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, artificial intelligence and climate change response.

Efforts should be made to promote friendship between the two countries through expanded people-to-people exchanges, Xi said, noting that the two sides had agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism.

For his part, Albanese said Australia and China share an interest in open and rules-based trade.

"The relationship that we are building is positive, is calm, is not defined by our differences, but one where we can have clear and frank exchanges for our mutual interest," he said.

The meeting with Albanese came as Xi pursued a packed schedule of bilateral meetings with foreign leaders in the aftermath of the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen.

Other leaders whom he met on Friday included prime ministers Lawrence Wong of Singapore, Anwar Ibrahim of Malaysia and Anutin Charnvirakul of Thailand as well as President Prabowo Subianto of Indonesia.

Wong congratulated Xi on his historic trilateral summit with Russia and the United States and said he was "looking to build on government-to-government initiatives to deepen our economic ties further", referring to projects in Suzhou, Tianjin and Chongqing.

In the meeting between Xi and Prabowo, the leaders announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership.

Xi said China and Indonesia should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust, and jointly guard against and respond to external risks.

He called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy. (Xinhua & Reuters)

Edited by Altis Wong

articles.title: HK can make contribution to construction sector: CE
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong is well placed to contribute to the national effort to enhance the construction sector's global standing and competitiveness…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong is well placed to contribute to the national effort to enhance the construction sector's global standing and competitiveness, Chief Executive John Lee said.

Lee said the national 15th Five-Year Plan calls for raising the construction sector's global standing, and that Hong Kong connects the country's capabilities with international opportunities while providing professional support to turn them into successful projects.

"In a world shaped by shifting geopolitics, urgent climate challenges, and rapid technological advance, insights alone are not enough. We must turn ideas into projects with lasting impact," he said at the opening ceremony of the inaugural InfraEX Week, which brings together some 800 infrastructure project leaders, government officials and professionals from over 30 countries and economies.

Lee said the SAR's first five-year plan, closely aligned with the national version, offers a strategic roadmap for the city's future while enabling Hong Kong to better integrate into and serve the overall national development.

A clear example, he said, is the Northern Metropolis, which takes up a third of Hong Kong's geographical area and will eventually be home to some 2.5 million people, create half a million jobs and account for about 13 percent of the city's GDP.

He said the Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Cooperation Zone and three planned university towns would integrate innovation, industry and education.

Lee said the city must deliver projects that are truly future-ready, and that means "quality, more than quantity."

"To build the Northern Metropolis and all that it promises, we must deliver infrastructure that is truly future-ready, and that means quality more than quantity."

He said artificial intelligence, advanced engineering technologies, construction robots and digital supervision systems are being deployed to improve productivity and cost-effectiveness.

Lee also highlighted the city's services expertise, spanning engineering, project management, legal and financial services, and cited a footbridge built with home-produced S960 high-strength steel as an example of Hong Kong's role as a super connector and super value-adder, bridging standards and validating innovation.

He added that collaboration would take concrete shape with the exchange of memorandums of understanding and a letter of intent with international and local partners.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Trump issues pardon to MLB hits king Pete Rose
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he has issued a posthumous pardon to Pete Rose, the controversial Major League…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he has issued a posthumous pardon to Pete Rose, the controversial Major League Baseball all-time hits leader who was convicted of tax evasion in 1990.

Rose, who died in 2024 at age 83, was a three-time World Series champion who set MLB records with 4,256 hits and 3,562 games played over the course of his career.

Rose was banned from baseball in 1989 after an investigation found he bet on baseball games, although he was reinstated last year by MLB commissioner Rob Manfred, who ruled lifetime bans expire upon the death of the person involved.

In 1990, Rose was convicted on two charges of filing false income tax returns by not declaring income he made from selling memorabilia and autographs. He served five months in a minimum security prison and was released in 1991.

"I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND, whose record of 4,256 Hits in a Season will never be broken," Trump posted on social media.

Trump got that wrong – Rose got those hits over the course of his career, not in one season.

Trump also noted Rose's absence from the Baseball Hall of Fame despite his record hits and games played totals due to his banishment. He said Rose was "treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame. Politics, I guess!"

This was the latest instance of Trump making free-wheeling use of his power to pardon people convicted of crimes.

In his second term he has issued notable ones, including more than 1,500 people charged with involvement in the January 6, 2021 insurrection at the US Capitol, former New York mayor Rudy Giuilani, former Illinois governor Rod Blagojevich and Michael Harris, co-founder of Death Row Records.

Manfred's reinstatement of Rose had already opened the door for him to have another chance to reach the Baseball Hall of Fame.

The Hall of Fame's veterans committee can consider Rose in the Classic Baseball category involving players whose contributions to the sport largely came before the 1980s.

That group is next scheduled to consider Hall of Fame candidates in December 2027. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Shelton into ATP Finals semis as Zverev stays perfect
articles.excerpt: Ben Shelton got his work done on Thursday, but had to wait for top-seeded Alexander Zverev to take one set…
articles.fullText:
Ben Shelton got his work done on Thursday, but had to wait for top-seeded Alexander Zverev to take one set over No. 6 seed Arthur Fils in order to punch his ticket to the semifinals of the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy.

The third-seeded Shelton edged Spain's Rafael Jodar, 7-6 (8), 7-5 and advanced when Zverev won the first set over Fils, 6-4.

The German, who went 3-0 in the John McEnroe group, polished off the Frenchman, 6-4, 7-6 (6).

Shelton is guaranteed to play second-seeded Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz (2-0), who has clinched the top spot in the Ivan Lendl group.

Zverev will play the winner of Friday's match between Russia's Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe.

The semifinal matches will take place on Saturday.

Jodar, the No. 8 seed, had the only break points early in the first set, but failed to capitalise on a pair in the fifth game. The 20-year old earned two set points on his serve in the tie-breaker, but did not come through and Shelton managed to prevail.

The players battled to 5-5 in the second set, but Shelton broke a fatiguing Jodar and came back from 15-30 to reach the semifinals in his first ATP Finals appearance.

Shelton cranked out 14 aces to only one double fault, but only got 57 percent of his first serves in and fended off 5 of 6 break points.

Not knowing his fate after the match, Shelton said, "Either way, it's been an incredible year for me. I'm happy with the way I competed throughout the year, the way I've bounced back after difficult things have happened and to win two matches here after making a deep run in Paris as well, I feel that I put a positive end to my season."

The servers dominated the first six games of the nightcap, but Zverev raced to a love-40 lead in Fils' fourth service game and earned the break at 30-40.

He won the first set to eliminate the 22-year old, but Fils battled until the end. He fought off five match points in the second set tie-breaker to get to 6-6, but Zverev recovered to improve to 65-18 on the season.

Zverev revealed that he was experiencing right ankle pain in his post-match comments. He suffered torn ligaments in that area in 2022 and is resigned to the fact that it will likely occasionally trouble him for the rest of his career.

"I'm going to do everything I can to be pain-free on Saturday, but this is something I have to live with nowadays," said Zverev. "I can still move well, but you can see immediately my serve speeds go down. I hope I'll be 100 percent on Saturday." (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Data broker opt-out steps retirees need before the holidays
articles.excerpt: A single data broker opt-out may not be enough. Spokeo, Whitepages and BeenVerified can still expose your address and family…
articles.fullText:
Many retirees think they're protecting their privacy by staying off social media, removing their information from one people-search site or paying for credit monitoring. But a single data broker opt-out request may leave your home address, phone number and family details exposed elsewhere. With the holidays approaching, now is a good time to find out what's available about you online and take steps to remove it.
People-search sites like Spokeo, Whitepages and BeenVerified can make personal details available to strangers. Some information is free to view, while more detailed reports may require payment. And here's where it gets concerning. A scammer who knows your grandson's name or where your daughter lives could use those details to make a fake emergency call sound convincing. Here's where that information comes from, how to remove it and what you can do to help protect your family before the holidays.

WHY CAREFUL PEOPLE STILL END UP ON DATA BROKER SITES
You don't need a social media account to have your information collected. Data brokers gather information from public records, including property deeds, voter registration records where accessible and court filings. They may also obtain details from commercial databases, online activity and companies that collect personal information. Over time, those details can become part of a profile showing where you live, previous addresses, phone numbers and possible family connections.
According to the Federal Trade Commission, opting out of one people-search site doesn't remove your information from others. Your details may also reappear when public records change or websites collect updated information. For older adults, the financial risks can be especially serious. An FTC report released in October 2026 found that adults ages 60 and older reported approximately $3 billion in fraud losses during 2025. Although older adults reported losing money to fraud less frequently than younger adults overall, their reported individual losses tended to be higher.
You can use a free exposure scanner at CyberGuy.com to check whether your personal information appears on publicly searchable websites. Keep in mind that a free scan cannot uncover every private data broker database. The results might surprise you.
You can start removing your personal information yourself without paying for a service.
A credit freeze won't remove your information from data brokers, and credit monitoring generally alerts you to possible problems rather than preventing your details from appearing online. These tools serve different purposes.
One thing to remember: Removing your information from people-search sites doesn't erase public records. Your details may still appear in property records, court documents or even listings connected to family members . That's why it's important to check more than your own name. Doing this yourself can take hours, especially when you're dealing with multiple websites. And because data brokers continue collecting information, the work may need to be repeated.
DATA BROKER OPT-OUT: HOW RETIREES CAN PROTECT THEIR DATA
Before paying for a data removal service, there are two other options worth knowing about.
Google offers a free tool called Results about you that can help you find personal information appearing in Google Search. Depending on eligibility, you may be able to request the removal of results containing your home address, phone number or email address.

Keep in mind that removing a Google search result doesn't delete the information from the original website. You may still need to contact the site directly.
If you live in California, you have another option. The state's free Delete Request and Opt-out Platform, called DROP, launched in January 2026. It allows eligible California residents to submit a single deletion request covering more than 600 registered data brokers.
Beginning Aug. 1, 2026, covered data brokers were required to start processing requests through the system. Removal can take time, and some information may be exempt under the law. You can submit a request and check its status at California's official DROP website at privacy.ca.gov/drop/. Other states also have privacy laws that may give residents additional rights to request deletion of their information.
WHY REMOVING YOUR DATA ONLINE MAY STILL LEAVE YOUR FAMILY EXPOSED
If you don't want to spend hours contacting websites and tracking removal requests, a personal data removal service can help.
These services contact data brokers on your behalf and submit requests to remove your personal information . Depending on the provider and plan, features may include:
Some services offer ongoing monitoring and follow-up requests, which can save time compared with handling each website yourself. It's important to understand that no service can guarantee every piece of personal information will disappear from the internet. Public records may remain accessible, and some websites may fall outside the service's coverage. Still, reducing the number of places where your information appears can make your personal details harder to find.
Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.
Thanksgiving brings families together, making it a great opportunity to talk about protecting everyone's personal information. You don't need to make it a lengthy discussion. A few simple checks can help everyone understand what scammers may already know about them.
After dinner, sit down with a family member and search your names on a few people-search sites. Look for home addresses, phone numbers and family connections. If you find something you don't want publicly available, discuss how to request its removal. Check your parents' information, too, with their permission. Even if you've removed your own details, your name or address may still appear in a relative's profile.
Choose a private phrase that family members can use if someone calls claiming there's an emergency. Avoid birthdays, pet names or other details someone could easily discover online. Agree on the phrase privately rather than sharing it in a group chat. A code word adds another layer of protection, but it shouldn't be your only way to verify someone's identity.
If someone claims to be a grandchild or another relative who urgently needs money, don't send anything until you've checked the story. Hang up and call your loved one directly using a phone number you already know. If you can't reach them, contact another trusted family member. Scammers can now use AI voice cloning to sound like someone you love. That means even a familiar voice may not be enough to prove who's calling. Learn more about how AI voice scams can clone your family's voice and what you can do to protect yourself. And be especially suspicious if someone demands payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or wire transfers.
Agree that nobody will send emergency money based solely on an unexpected phone call or text. If something sounds suspicious, contact another family member before taking action. Scammers often pressure people to respond immediately or keep the situation secret. The more your family talks about these tactics ahead of time, the easier it becomes to recognize a suspicious request . Scammers may already know more about your family than you realize. A private code word adds protection, but always confirm an unexpected emergency by contacting your loved one directly before sending money.
Here's what concerns me. You can be careful about what you share online and still have your home address, phone number and family details available on people-search sites. Removing that information once is a good start, but it can show up again. That's why I recommend checking these sites regularly or using a trusted data removal service to help handle the work. And with Thanksgiving bringing families together, this is a great time to talk about scams and make sure everyone knows what to do if a suspicious call comes in. A few simple steps now could help keep your family's personal information out of the wrong hands.

articles.title: World Court finds Myanmar responsible for Rohingya genocide in landmark ruling
articles.excerpt: Experts say the judgment marks a historic victory for the Rohingya but enforcement remains a challenge.
articles.fullText:
Updated on Nov. 19, 2026 at 11:21 a.m. ET
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, in a landmark judgment that could increase diplomatic pressure on its military-led government.
In a 9-6 decision, the United Nations’ top court found that Myanmar had violated the 1948 Genocide Convention during a military crackdown that drove more than 730,000 Rohingya to neighboring Bangladesh in 2017.
It was the first time the court had found a state responsible for committing genocide.
The judgment comes as Myanmar’s President Min Aung Hlaing, who commanded the military during the crackdown, seeks to restore his country’s international standing.
“This is a historic ruling. For the first time, the world court has found a state responsible for committing genocide – and the man who commanded those operations is now Myanmar’s president,” Richard Horsey, senior adviser for Asia at the Belgium-based International Crisis Group, said in a statement.
“The Rohingya have waited nine years to hear a court say this. It will not change their lives quickly, but it puts what was done to them on the legal record, and no amount of denial in Naypyidaw can remove it.”
UN top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said evidence showed that Myanmar’s security forces had killed some 10,000 Rohingya during the crackdown.
“The Court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya ⁠civilians, perpetrated widespread acts ⁠of sexual violence as well as acts of ⁠extreme violence against children and ⁠attacked fleeing Rohingya ⁠as they sought to flee in large numbers to ‌Bangladesh,” Iwasawa said.
The court concluded that the only reasonable inference from the evidence was that Myanmar’s security forces intended to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population.
It also found that Myanmar had failed to fulfill its obligation to prevent genocide.
The case was brought in 2019 by The Gambia, which accused Myanmar of violating the Genocide Convention and sought to hold the Southeast Asian nation accountable for atrocities against the predominantly Muslim ethnic minority.
Myanmar has maintained that its military operations were in response to attacks on police posts by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, a Rohingya armed group.
Diplomatic pressure
While the judgment establishes Myanmar’s legal responsibility for genocide, questions remain over its practical consequences and whether other governments will reconsider their engagement with Naypyitaw.
“Governments rolling out the red carpet for Min Aung Hlaing will now be doing so for the head of a state found responsible for genocide. Most will carry on regardless, but it will be harder to present this as business as usual,” Horsey said.
“The court has no means of enforcing this ruling. What matters now is whether the governments engaging Naypyitaw are prepared to attach any cost to ignoring it.”
Myanmar's Union Minister for the Ministry of the President's Office Ko Ko Hlaing attends a hearing on the day the International Court of Justice delivers its judgment in the case brought by Gambia accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority, in The Hague, Netherlands, Nov. 19, 2026.
(Piroschka Van De Wouw/Reuters) Horsey added that the ruling was likely to make Myanmar’s government more defensive in its dealings with the United Nations as it sought to regain its seat at the world body.
Human rights advocates called on governments to use the judgment to press Myanmar to end abuses against the Rohingya.
“The International Court of Justice’s landmark ruling is long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military. The ruling also provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice,” Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at New York-based Human Rights Watch, said in a statement.
In response to the ruling, the United Kingdom will order the expulsion of the Myanmar defense attaché and call on the U.N. Security Council to address it, the UK’s foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said in a statement.
“The Rohingya have endured years of appalling violence, displacement and persecution.” Miliband said. “Myanmar must comply fully with the judgement. The international community must now play its part in supporting implementation, accountability, and justice for the Rohingya.”
Uncertain future for refugees
The ruling comes amid a humanitarian crisis compounded by renewed fighting in Myanmar’s western Rakhine state, where the military has lost control of large areas to the Arakan Army, an ethnic Rakhine armed group.
“Most of the land the Rohingya fled is now held by the Arakan Army, an ethnic Rakhine armed group fighting Naypyitaw. For Rohingya still in Myanmar’s Rakhine State, how the Arakan Army treats them will matter more than anything Naypyitaw says,” Horsey said.
A Rohingya refugee gives a thumbs up while another person holds a placard following the announcement of the International Court of Justice verdict, at a refugee camp in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, Nov. 19, 2026.
(Mohammad Ponir Hossain/REUTERS) Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya remain in refugee camps in Bangladesh, where international aid funding cuts have led to reductions in food rations.
“Hopefully this ruling will be a reminder of their plight to donors, who need to step up,” Horsey said.
Vignoli urged the international community to ensure that the ruling translated into tangible improvements for the persecuted minority.
“Myanmar should swiftly comply with the court’s judgment and end its oppression of the Rohingya. Concerned governments should strongly support the Rohingya and promote justice for atrocities, press Myanmar’s junta to comply with the judgment, and ensure the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.
Update adds Miliband’s statement.

Primary One discretionary places for September 2027 will be released next Monday, the Education Bureau announced today.

Of the 32,104 children who applied for discretionary places at government and aided primary schools, 18,148 will be offered a place.

Among them, 8,270 have siblings studying or parents working at the schools they have applied to. The remaining 9,878 have been selected according to the Points System.

Parents who have already activated their Primary One Admission e-Platform (ePOA) account can check the results via the e-platform from 10am on Monday.
